Because surviving in the stock market is mainly about skill, not capital: a skilled person only needs 48 successful trades to turn 20,000 into 100 million; meanwhile, turning 100 million into 20,000 requires no skill and doesn't take long either. Capital sets your starting point, but ability sets your destination. You use small capital as a fig leaf, refusing to admit—what's really holding you back is that your skills haven't grown.

qa.q: 你交易時，是為了「賺錢」，還是為了「手癢想交易」？本書把什麼列為第一重點？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 你手癢了，隨手買進一筆，說不出這次要賺什麼、停在哪。投資股票的目的是賺錢。交易之初雖是為賺錢，多次失敗後人們常淡忘目的，變成只為交易的願望而買賣，沒有目標、寄望僥倖，註定失敗。你買的不是機會，是手癢本身；寄望僥倖那一刻，早就忘了進場是為了賺錢。
qa.a_en: Heyyy~ 😊 Your hands itch, you casually buy something, and you can't even say what you're trying to make or where you'll stop. The purpose of stock investing is to make money. Sure, at first you trade to make money, but after repeated failures people often forget the goal—they just trade for the sake of trading, no target, hoping for luck, and that's destined to fail. What you're buying isn't an opportunity, it's the itch itself; the moment you hope for luck, you've already forgotten you entered to make money.

qa.q: 你會不會在下單那一刻就知道「這次沒把握，賭一把」？本書說這種交易從哪裡就開始錯了？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 你下單前明明心裡沒底，卻還是按了確認，賭一把。因為沒有做過充分準備、目的不明確的交易，從開始的那一刻就已經錯了；把每次交易寄望於僥倖，事後結果往往又是失敗，虧錢成為一種習慣。模糊的希望，是虧損的溫牀。你用「賭一把」掩蓋沒準備；這種模糊的希望，養成了虧錢的習慣還不自知。
qa.a_en: Heyyy~ 😊 Before placing the order, you know deep down you're not confident, but you hit confirm anyway—just gambling. Because a trade made without adequate preparation and a clear purpose is already wrong from the moment it starts; when you pin every trade on luck, the outcome is usually another failure, and losing money becomes a habit. Vague hope is the breeding ground for losses. You use "just gambling" to cover for being unprepared; this kind of vague hope trains you into a losing-money habit without you even knowing it.

qa.q: 要怎麼做，纔不會在連虧三次之後，忘了自己為什麼進股市？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 你設過「沒把握不下單」的規矩，真到盤前卻總忘了念。從現在開始記住，並在每次交易發生之前不斷提醒自己：股票交易的目的是賺錢，沒有把握賺錢的交易請不要發生。提醒不是口號，是下單前的最後一道閘門。你不是不知道規矩，是手癢時總想繞過那道閘門——繞一次，規矩就輕了一分。
keywords: 纔不會在連虧三次之後
忘了自己為什麼進股市
qa.a_en: Heyyy~ 😊 You once set a rule: "No order unless I'm confident." But when the chart's right in front of you, you always forget to say it. Starting now, remember it, and before every trade, keep reminding yourself: the purpose of stock trading is to make money, and if you're not confident you'll make money, then don't let that trade happen. Reminding isn't a slogan—it's the last gate before hitting the button. It's not that you don't know the rule; it's that when your hands itch, you always try to sneak past that gate—and every time you sneak past once, the rule weighs a little less.

qa.q: 你敢不敢合上書，把自己的交易歷史一筆一筆寫出來？本章要求你先做哪件事？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 你盤後跟人侃侃而談虧在哪，卻從沒真正落下筆。合上書本不再往下讀，回憶交易歷程與現狀，反省過往交易，並用筆認真寫下自省問題的答案，例如交易次數、買賣依據等，總結過去以迎接全新未來。寫下來，纔看得見。你寧可嘴上反省，不肯寫下來，是因為白紙黑字要你當場承認錯——你躲著它。
keywords: 本章要求你先做哪件事
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 You love talking after hours about where you lost money, but you never actually put pen to paper. Close the books, stop reading, look back at your trading journey and where you are now, reflect on past trades, and seriously write down your answers to self-reflection questions—like how many trades you made, what your buy/sell reasons were, etc. Sum up the past to welcome a brand-new future. Write it down—only then can you see it. You'd rather reflect out loud than write it down, because putting it in black and white forces you to admit your mistakes on the spot—and you're dodging that.

qa.q: 如果把你的交易史當成考卷，你答得出哪幾題——交易過幾次、依據是什麼、聽過誰的話？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 書單要你盤點買賣依據，你卻草草填了幾個數字交差。包括交易總次數、每次交易前是否明確目的是賺錢、買入與賣出股票的依據、是否賣後股價即漲、是否因聽人勸說放棄自己的選擇、一年前賣掉的股票漲幅、對財務報表的看法及帳戶盈虧等。你隨手填，是怕認真算會照出自己的亂；承認沒依據，比多填幾行難。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 The checklist asks you to review your buy/sell reasons, but you just scribbled a few numbers to get it done. Things like total number of trades, whether you had a clear goal of making money before each trade, the reasons for buying and selling stocks, whether the price went up right after you sold, whether you gave up your own choice because someone talked you into it, how much a stock you sold a year ago has risen, your take on financial statements, and your account P&L. You filled it in carelessly because you're afraid that taking it seriously would expose your own chaos; admitting you had no basis is harder than filling in a few extra lines.

qa.q: 你還在為去年的虧損懊悔嗎？本書說過去該怎麼處理？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 你睡前又翻出去年那筆大虧，越想越悶。無論現在的狀況是懊悔、迷茫還是沮喪，一切已成過去；總結過去是為了有全新的未來，把不愉快經歷忘記，讓我們重新有一個全新的開始。懊悔是重複付利息，總結纔是提款。你以為在總結，其實是在重溫不甘；一口氣悶在心裡，總結永遠翻不了頁。
keywords: 本書說過去該怎麼處理
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 Before bed, you keep flipping back to that big loss from last year, and the more you think, the more suffocated you feel. Whatever state you're in now—regret, confusion, or frustration—it's all in the past. Summing up the past is for having a brand-new future; forget the unpleasant experiences and let's start fresh. Regret is paying interest on the same debt over and over; only a true summary lets you withdraw. You think you're summarizing, but you're actually reliving the resentment—that knot stays stuck in your chest, and your summary never turns the page.

qa.q: 「走得太遠，以至於忘記了出發的目的」——這句話說的是書裡的人，還是鏡子裡的你？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 你天天忙著看盤買賣，卻想不起當初為什麼進來。以「走得太遠，以至於我們忘記了出發的目的」比喻：多次失敗的交易之後，人們漸漸淡忘交易是為了賺錢的初衷，只為交易願望而買賣。走得越久，越要回頭看初衷。你被手癢推著走，離初衷愈遠愈不肯回頭——回頭就要承認，自己早忘了為何而來。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 You're busy every day watching the charts and trading, but you can't remember why you even started. It's like the saying, 'We've walked so far that we forgot where we set out from.' After many failed trades, people gradually lose sight of the original goal—trading to make money—and just trade for the sake of trading. The longer you walk, the more you need to look back at your original intention. You're pushed along by itchy fingers, and the further you drift from your goal, the more you refuse to look back—because looking back would mean admitting you've long forgotten why you came.

qa.q: 你以為成為好投資人需要的是內幕、資金還是運氣？本書給的清單是什麼？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 你讀到這份清單，點點頭，轉頭照舊懶得做。需要有所準備：牢記交易目的是賺錢、每次交易前確立目標、反省過往交易歷史、忘掉過去失敗，為了賺錢從頭開始。四件事，沒有一件靠運氣。你不是不懂，是寧可賭那口僥倖，也不肯老實動手準備。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 You read this list, nod your head, then turn around and go back to being lazy as usual. There are things you need to prepare: keep in mind that the purpose of trading is to make money, set a goal before every trade, reflect on your past trading history, forget past failures, and start over from scratch for the sake of making money. Four things—none of them rely on luck. It's not that you don't understand; it's that you'd rather gamble on that bit of luck than honestly get down to preparing.

qa.q: 同樣是「壟斷」，為什麼當消費者時你恨它，當股東時你愛它？本書怎麼解釋這個雙面性？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 你買東西罵壟斷，買股票卻處處找壟斷。壟斷使商品資源趨於稀缺、價格上漲，對消費者如魔鬼，須付出幾倍於實際價格的金錢；但對投資領域如天使，因壟斷可自由決定價格，使自身利益最大化。你當消費者罵、當股東愛，是雙重標準——怕承認自己只愛能漲的那一面。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 You curse monopolies when you're buying things, but when you're buying stocks, you go hunting for monopolies everywhere. A monopoly makes goods and resources scarcer and drives prices up—like a devil to consumers, who have to pay several times the real price. But in the investment world, it's like an angel, because a monopoly can freely set prices to maximize its own profit. You curse as a consumer and love it as a shareholder—that's a double standard. You're afraid to admit that you only love the side that can go up.

qa.q: 你猜主力資金最常用的控盤手段是什麼？本書說與「壟斷」有什麼關係？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 你看到股價莫名往上竄，只顧跟不跟，從沒想過籌碼在誰手裡。因為操縱股價的主力資金正是透過壟斷所要操縱股票的流通籌碼來控制價格、實現利益最大化，故壟斷與股價漲跌直接掛鉤，是股市中最常見的現象。你懶得想「誰壟斷」，是怕一想就發現自己只是跟在後頭的——逃避這問，追高就追得心安。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 You see a stock price mysteriously shooting up, and all you care about is whether to follow it—never once thinking about whose hands the chips are in. Because the main funds manipulating a stock are precisely using a monopoly on the floating chips of that stock to control the price and maximize profits. So monopoly is directly linked to price swings—it's the most common phenomenon in the stock market. You can't be bothered to ask 'who's monopolizing it,' because you're afraid that if you did, you'd realize you're just the one following behind—avoid that question, and you can chase highs with an easy conscience.

qa.q: 主力是怎麼讓一隻股票「想漲就漲」的？本書說的關鍵動作是什麼？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 你買一隻，從沒查過它的籌碼集中還是分散。主力資金壟斷所要操縱股票的流通籌碼，使投向市場的籌碼資源趨於稀缺，從而自由決定價格，讓自身利益最大化。籌碼在手，價格隨心。你跳過這一查，是圖省事——真查了怕看出籌碼散了、價格攥不在強者手裡，自己那筆就站不穩。
keywords: 主力是怎麼讓一隻股票
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 You buy a stock without ever checking whether its chips are concentrated or scattered. Main funds monopolize the floating chips of the stock they want to manipulate, making the chips available to the market scarce, so they can freely set the price and maximize their own profit. Chips in hand, price at will. You skip that check to save yourself the trouble—but if you actually checked, you'd be afraid to see the chips scattered and the price not firmly in the hands of the strong, and then your own position wouldn't stand steady.

qa.q: 如果你只能看一個數據來判斷股價方向，本書建議你看什麼？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 你盯著股價猜漲跌，卻從不盯籌碼集中還是分散。流通籌碼越集中，說明投向市場的資源越來越稀缺，股價將越來越高；籌碼越分散，說明資源越來越豐富，價格自然下降，故集中度可指示漲跌方向。你懶得看這一項，是怕看出籌碼在散——承認持倉在鬆動，比看股價跌還難受。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 You stare at stock prices guessing ups and downs, but you never watch whether chips are concentrated or scattered. The more concentrated the floating chips, the scarcer the resources flowing into the market, and the higher the stock price goes; the more scattered the chips, the more abundant the resources, and prices naturally fall—so concentration can indicate the direction of movement. You don't bother with this one because you're afraid you'll see the chips scattering—admitting your position is loosening hurts worse than watching the price drop.

qa.q: 為什麼「沒人賣」的股票反而漲？本書用什麼原理解釋？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 你納悶「明明沒人賣，它卻一直漲」，卻說不出所以然。流通籌碼越集中，代表投向市場的資源越來越稀缺，資源稀缺使價格上漲，如同壟斷商品價格高漲的原理，故集中度上升預示股價上升。你答不出籌碼趨勢，是怕認真查會露怯——把漲當成運氣，比承認自己沒看懂輕鬆。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 You're puzzled, "No one's selling, why does it keep going up?" but you can't explain why. The more concentrated the floating chips, the scarcer the resources flowing into the market, and scarcity drives prices up—just like how monopoly goods are priced high. So rising concentration signals a rising stock price. You can't answer the chip trend because you're afraid that digging deeper will expose you—treating the rise as luck is easier than admitting you don't really get it.

qa.q: 什麼信號出現時，你該警惕手上的股票要跌了？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 指標亮出籌碼在散，你卻對自己說「再等等看」。流通籌碼越來越分散，說明投向市場的資源越來越豐富，資源豐富了價格自然就要下降，故籌碼分散預示股價下跌。你選「再等等」，是捨不得那點帳面紅——承認要跌，就等於承認自己該賣在更早。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 The indicator shows chips are scattering, but you tell yourself, "Let's wait a little longer." The more dispersed the floating chips, the more abundant the resources flowing into the market, and when resources are abundant, prices naturally fall—so scattered chips signal a price drop. You choose to "wait" because you can't let go of those paper gains—admitting it's going to drop means admitting you should've sold earlier.

qa.q: 同樣一個詞，為什麼消費者和投資者感受完全不同？本書說關鍵在於什麼？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 你同一張嘴，買菜罵壟斷、買股找壟斷。壟斷對消費者是可怕的魔鬼，令消費者付出幾倍於實際價格的金錢；對投資者卻是天使，因可自由決定價格並最大化利益，關鍵在於身處消費還是投資立場。你分不清自己的立場，是貪那能漲的一面——利益當前，道理就讓了路。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 Same mouth, you curse monopolies at the grocery store but chase them when buying stocks. A monopoly is a terrifying devil for consumers, making them pay several times the actual price; but for investors, it's an angel, because it can freely set prices and maximize profits—it all depends on whether you're on the consumer side or the investment side. You can't tell your own position because you're greedy for the side that goes up—when profits are in front of you, logic steps aside.

qa.q: 你下一次選股，會把「籌碼集中度」放在第幾順位？本書給的方法要點是什麼？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 你下次選股，記得把籌碼集中度排進清單。觀察個股流通籌碼的集中程度：集中度升高代表資源稀缺、價格看漲，籌碼分散則看跌，以此判斷股價變動方向並作出投資決策。你上次買入前跳過這項，是圖快——真把它當第一關，想必能擋掉好幾筆衝動的單。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 Next time you pick stocks, remember to put chip concentration on your checklist. Watch the concentration level of the stock's floating chips: rising concentration means scarce resources and a bullish outlook, while scattered chips point down. Use that to judge price direction and make decisions. You skipped this step before buying last time because you wanted speed—if you really made it the first gate, it would've blocked quite a few impulsive trades.

qa.q: 你會去「追」籌碼集中的股票，還是等它啟動？本書說壟斷邏輯怎麼用？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 你總是等它漲起來，才後悔「早該看籌碼集中度」。應留意流通籌碼集中程度高的個股，集中度越高代表壟斷籌碼越充分、價格越可能上漲，可作為發現股價變動方向與選股的參考指標。你漲後纔想起這邏輯，是手癢等不及——在啟動前上車要忍，你寧可漲了再追，也不肯先蹲著等。
keywords: 本書說壟斷邏輯怎麼用
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 You always wait until it's already risen, then regret, "I should've checked chip concentration earlier." Keep an eye on stocks with highly concentrated floating chips—the higher the concentration, the more complete the monopoly over chips and the more likely the price will rise. It can serve as a reference for spotting price direction and stock selection. You only think of this logic after it goes up because your hands were itching—getting on board before the move takes patience, and you'd rather chase the rally than squat and wait.

qa.q: 你買一支股票前，做過「價值評估」嗎？還是覺得「研究基本面太難」？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 基本面選股就是對你打算投資的股票進行全方位的價值評估，評估方法很多（如方差等），核心是全面評估股票的投資價值。你說太難，是因為你把「全面」想成「完美」——書裡要的只是抓住關鍵，而你用「太難」擋住了自己踏出第一步。你怕承認，難是逃避的藉口。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 Fundamental stock picking is about doing a full value assessment of the stock you're planning to invest in. There are many methods (like variance, etc.), but the core is thoroughly evaluating the stock's investment value. You say it's too hard because you've confused "comprehensive" with "perfect"—what the books really want is just to grab the key points, but you've used "too hard" to block yourself from taking the first step. You're afraid to admit that difficulty is just an excuse to run away.

qa.q: 你覺得自己分析不了基本面，是因為「不夠專業」嗎？——還是因為你根本拿不到信息？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 主要困難不是專業知識問題，而是獲取有效信息的途徑較為單一，不可能拿到多少有價值的信息，因此需要化繁為簡地運用基本面選股。你把困難歸咎於「不夠專業」，是在給自己找一個體面的藉口——真正難的是承認：你缺的不是智商，是信息渠道。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 The main difficulty isn't a matter of professional knowledge—it's that your channels for getting useful information are too narrow, so you can't obtain much valuable data. That's why you need to simplify and use fundamental stock picking. You blame it on "not being professional enough," and that's giving yourself a respectable excuse—the real hard part is admitting: it's not your IQ that's lacking, it's your info channels.

qa.q: 一份財報擺在你面前，你能說出該看哪四樣嗎？還是看到數字就頭暈？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 主要看四方面：最近3年的淨資產收益率、最近3年的淨資產增減情況以及現在的淨資產值、企業在行業內所處的地位、企業的股本結構。財報像體檢報告，你不用看懂每一項，只要盯住關鍵指標——你頭暈，是因為你想全看懂，而高手只抓重點。你怕承認，自己總想全看懂。
keywords: 你能說出該看哪四樣嗎
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 Mainly look at four things: the return on net assets over the last 3 years, how net assets have changed in those 3 years and their current value, the company's position in its industry, and its shareholding structure. Financial reports are like a health check-up—you don't have to understand every item, just keep your eye on the key numbers. The reason you're dizzy is that you're trying to read everything, while pros just grab the essentials. You're afraid to admit you always want to understand it all.

qa.q: 你自己研究不好基本面——你願意「借機構的腦子」嗎？還是覺得丟臉？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 充分研究介入股票的資金類型，選擇有基金、社保、券商等大機構介入的股票。因為大機構介入前大都對上市公司基本面做過專業價值評估，借機構之智可完成投資價值評估。你不願借力，是因為你覺得「跟著機構買」顯得不聰明——可市場不獎勵聰明，只獎勵正確。你怕承認，自己放不下聰明。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 Do a deep dive into the types of money flowing into a stock, and pick ones that have big institutions like funds, social security, and brokerages involved. Because before those big guys step in, they've usually done a professional valuation of the basics—so you can borrow their brainpower to gauge the value. You won't lean on that because you think 'following the institutions' makes you look less smart. But the market doesn't reward being smart—it rewards being right. You're afraid to admit you can't let go of feeling smart.

qa.q: 熱點板塊出現時，你是追進去，還是先問「它為什麼熱」？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 某一段時間內證券市場一定會有某個行業整體成為熱點的狀況，通常稱為熱點板塊，可作為基本面選股的重要參考方向。熱點是結果不是原因——你追熱點而不問邏輯，等於看到煙火就衝，卻不知道火藥在哪裡。你怕承認，追熱是貪快錢。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 At any stretch of time, some industry is bound to become the market's hot sector—we call it a hot theme. You can use that as a key reference for fundamental picking. But hot is the effect, not the cause. Chasing a theme without asking the logic is like running at a firework without knowing where the powder is. You're afraid to admit that chasing heat is just greed for fast money.

qa.q: 重大事件來臨時，你的第一反應是「跟我有什麼關係」，還是「這是機會還是風險」？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 很多重大事件很可能是一次千載難逢的機遇，應特別關注身邊有可能影響經濟環境以及企業經營環境的大事件，這樣有可能抓住巨大的機會。你對大事麻木，是因為你習慣了「事不關己」——可投資裡，所有的大事最終都會變成你帳戶裡的數字。你怕承認，自己對大事麻木。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 Tons of major events are likely once-in-a-lifetime chances. You should really keep an eye on the big things around you that could change the economy or the business environment—that's how you grab massive opportunities. The reason you're numb to them is that you're used to 'not my business.' But in investing, every big event eventually becomes numbers in your account. You're afraid to admit you're numb to the big stuff.

qa.q: 你關心過「影響經濟環境」的大事件嗎？還是隻關心自己那幾支股票？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 關注有可能影響經濟環境以及企業經營環境的大事件，重大事件常帶來千載難逢的機遇，把握住可能獲取巨大收益。只看個股不看大局，等於只看自家院子不看天氣——暴風雨來的時候，院子裡的人最後知道。你怕承認，自己常是最後知道的人。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 Pay attention to the big events that could affect the economy and how companies operate. Major events often carry rare opportunities, and if you seize one, the payoff can be huge. If you only look at your stock and ignore the whole market, it's like watching your own yard and never checking the weather—when the storm hits, the people in the yard are the last to know. You're afraid to admit you're usually the last one to find out.

qa.q: 信息拿不到、專業比不過——你願意承認「有人比我懂」並跟著他們嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 鑒於獲取上市公司信息能力有限，可通過瞭解基金、券商、QFII等機構的介入情況，分析判斷機構的專業評估，從而實現對上市公司投資價值的評估。承認「有人比我懂」不是認輸，是繞過自己的短板——你死撐著自己研究，撐到最後往往是用虧損交學費。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 Since you can't easily get all the info on a listed company, you can look at what funds, brokerages, and QFII are doing with it, read their professional judgment, and use that to value the company. Admitting 'someone knows better than me' isn't surrendering—it's getting around your own weak spot. But you stubbornly force yourself to research everything alone, and in the end, the losses are your tuition. You're afraid to admit you'd rather die on that hill.

qa.q: 學技術面選股，你是從「絕招」學起，還是從「注意事項」學起？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 應從技術面選股的注意事項入手，因為技術面選股內容最豐富但描述最困難，作者只針對注意事項談自己的看法。你總想先學絕招，因為絕招給你快感；但注意事項纔是防坑的——先學絕招的人，通常先把坑踩一遍。你怕承認，自己也愛先學絕招。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 We should start with the cautions for picking stocks based on technicals. The technical side is the richest area but the hardest to describe, and the author only speaks to the warnings. You always want the killer tricks first, because they give you a rush. But it's the warnings that protect you from traps. Those who go for tricks first usually step right into every trap. You're scared to admit you love the tricks first too.

qa.q: 你判斷一支股票，先看個股還是先看大盤？——你上一次買股，大盤是什麼趨勢？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 不僅要判斷所選個股的趨勢，更重要的是判斷當時的大盤趨勢，因為大勢決定一切。你只盯個股，等於在退潮的海灘上研究自己那塊石頭——大勢退潮時，再美的個股也擱淺。你怕承認，自己總在研究擱淺的石頭。
keywords: 先看個股還是先看大盤
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 You don't just have to judge the trend of the stock you picked—more importantly, judge the market trend at the time, because the big trend decides everything. If you only stare at your stock, that's like studying your rock on the beach as the tide goes out—when the tide recedes, even the prettiest stock gets stranded. You're afraid to admit you keep studying stranded rocks.

qa.q: 你看圖，是固定用一個週期，還是「打開哪個算哪個」？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 判斷趨勢需要注意判斷趨勢的週期，作者主張先用周線分析週期，再用日線的分析週期進行評估篩選。週期決定你看到的是樹還是森林——你用錯週期，等於用顯微鏡看地圖，看得再清楚也是錯的。你怕承認，自己用錯了鏡頭。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 To read the trend, you need to pay attention to the timeframe you're looking at. The author suggests first using the weekly chart to analyze the cycle, then using the daily chart to evaluate and filter. The timeframe decides whether you see the tree or the forest—if you use the wrong timeframe, it's like using a microscope to read a map. No matter how clearly you see it, it's still wrong. You're afraid to admit that you've been using the wrong lens.

qa.q: 你給過「周線走好」這條標準足夠的分量嗎？還是總被日線的波動牽著走？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 先用周線對所有目標股票的趨勢進行一次全面評估，凡是周線趨勢走好的股票，可以列為重點關注的對象。日線負責波動，周線負責方向——你被日線牽著走，等於讓噪音替你決定方向。你怕承認，自己總讓噪音帶路。
keywords: 這條標準足夠的分量嗎
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 Start by doing a full trend check on all your target stocks using the weekly chart. Any stock with a solid weekly trend should be put on your watchlist. The daily chart handles the noise, the weekly chart handles the direction—if you let the daily chart pull you around, you're letting noise make your decisions for you. You're afraid to admit that you always let the noise lead the way.

qa.q: 周線篩出重點、日線落實到具體股票——這個「先粗後細」的流程，你走過嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 在周線評估出重點關注對象後，再用日線的分析週期對全部重點關注對象進行評估篩選，最終落實到某隻股票。先粗後細是為了不讓細節幹擾方向——你跳過周線直接看日線，等於跳過戰略直接打戰術。你怕承認，自己總跳過戰略。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 After the weekly chart helps you pick out your watchlist, then switch to the daily chart to evaluate and filter all those candidates, and finally narrow it down to a specific stock. Going from the big picture to the details is so the details don't mess with your direction—if you skip the weekly chart and jump straight to the daily, it's like skipping strategy and going straight to tactics. You're afraid to admit that you always skip the strategy.

qa.q: 買一支股票前，你對「它該值多少錢」心中有數嗎？還是一路買一路猜？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 對現有價格進行合理化估計是必需的條件，只有做到對價位心中有數，才能知道什麼價位可以買、什麼價位有風險。心裡沒數就下單，等於不知道水深就跳——你以為是勇敢，其實是魯莽。你怕承認，自己常把魯莽當勇敢。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 It's a must to make a reasonable estimate of the current price. Only when you have a clear sense of the price level can you know what price is okay to buy and what price carries risk. Placing an order without knowing where you stand is like jumping into water without knowing how deep it is—you think it's brave, but it's actually reckless. You're afraid to admit that you often mistake recklessness for bravery.

qa.q: 你知道自己持倉的股票，三年來多在什麼價位區間活動嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 觀察該股最近3年的股價運行，統計低價區和高價區出現的次數，據此推算其投機合理區域。一支股票有自己的「脾氣」——你從不統計，是因為你覺得「這次會不一樣」；可統計的意義，正是提醒你「它大概率還是老樣子」。你怕承認，自己不愛看老樣子。
keywords: 你知道自己持倉的股票
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 Look at how the stock has been trading over the past 3 years, count how many times it hit the low zone and the high zone, and use that to figure out its reasonable speculative range. Every stock has its own 'temperament'—you never keep track because you think 'this time will be different.' But the whole point of keeping track is to remind you that 'it'll probably be the same old story.' You're afraid to admit that you don't like looking at the same old story.

qa.q: 10元以下是價值區、30元以上是風險區——你會在風險區追高嗎？你上次追高時知道那是風險區嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 若某股3年內10元以下出現不足3次（約1年1次）、30元以上只出現2次（約1.5年1次），則10元以下是可投機的價值區域，30元以上屬於風險區。區間擺在那裡，你卻總在風險區裡找「突破的理由」——不是區間錯了，是你不想承認自己在追高。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 If a stock has appeared below 10 yuan less than 3 times in 3 years (roughly once a year), and above 30 yuan only 2 times (roughly once every 1.5 years), then below 10 yuan is a speculative value zone, and above 30 yuan is a danger zone. The range is right there, but you're always looking for 'reasons to break out' inside the danger zone—it's not the range that's wrong, it's that you don't want to admit you're chasing highs.

qa.q: 「雞肋」區間——食之無味、棄之可惜。你手裡有幾支「雞肋」股？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 該股大部分時間維持在20元左右，20元附近基本上就屬於「雞肋」，即投機價值不大但又不算危險的區域。雞肋股最大的成本不是虧損，是佔用——你的資金和注意力被它綁住，真正的機會來了你也騰不出手。你怕承認，自己被雞肋綁住。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 If the stock mostly stays around 20 yuan, then the 20 yuan neighborhood is basically 'chicken ribs'—not much speculative value, but not exactly dangerous either. The biggest cost of a chicken-rib stock isn't the loss, it's the tie-up—your capital and attention get stuck on it, and when a real opportunity comes, you can't free up your hands. You're afraid to admit that you're tied up by chicken ribs.

qa.q: 電腦幫你選出的股票，你敢直接買嗎？——你知道它只是「半成品」嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 電腦自動選股是純粹的技術面選股，以技術指標為條件、事先設定程式自動篩選。因屬純技術選股，必須結合基本面選股再做最後篩選，才能提高選股勝率。你以為機器比人強，其實機器只會看圖——它不知道公司會不會倒，而你偷懶，它就替你把風險放大。你怕承認，自己偷懶信機器。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 Computer auto-picking is purely technical screening—it uses technical indicators as conditions, with a pre-set program that filters automatically. Since it's purely technical, you have to combine it with fundamental screening for a final pass to improve your win rate. You think the machine is better than you, but the machine only knows how to read charts—it doesn't know whether the company will go under, and if you get lazy, it just amplifies the risk for you. You're afraid to admit that you're lazy and trust the machine.

qa.q: 基本面選好的股票，你怎麼找買點？——等它漲了才追，還是讓電腦幫你盯？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 可以用電腦選股技術對事先用基本面選好的股票進行追蹤，藉此找到最佳的介入點，兼顧基本面與進場時機。好公司也要好價位——你只選公司不管時機，等於買了好房子卻在最高點接盤。你怕承認，自己從不算時機。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 You can use technical stock screening to track stocks you've already picked based on fundamentals, so you can find the best entry point—balancing both fundamentals and timing. A good company deserves a good price—if you only pick the company and ignore the timing, it's like buying a great house but catching it at the very top. You're afraid to admit you never really think about timing.

qa.q: 一個「一年只操作一次、至少八成資金」的方案——你受得了這種無聊嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 這是最保守的長線投機，資金運作週期只有一次操作機會，追求資金安全，適閤中小機構、老年及業餘投資人，投入資金應至少佔總資金的80%。你受不了無聊，是因為你把「操作」當成「賺錢」——可對很多人來說，少動纔是最大的盈利。你怕承認，自己動是怕無聊。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 This is the most conservative long-term speculation. The capital cycle only has one operation opportunity, prioritizing capital safety. It suits small to mid-sized institutions, older investors, and amateur investors. Allocated capital should be at least 80% of your total. You can't stand boredom because you confuse "trading" with "making money"—but for many people, doing less is exactly what brings the biggest profits. You're afraid to admit you trade just to cure the boredom.

qa.q: 一個週期操作2到4次——你上個月操作了幾次？超出了幾倍？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 它介乎長線與短線之間，兼顧利益最大化與資金相對安全，一個資金運作週期至少操作2次、通常以4次為標準，適合大部分投資人的需求。次數是設計出來的紀律——你超過次數，不是因為機會多，是因為手癢多。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 It sits between long-term and short-term, balancing maximum profit with relative capital safety. One capital cycle involves at least 2 operations, usually 4 as the standard, fitting most investors' needs. The number of trades is a discipline by design—when you exceed it, it's not because there are more opportunities, it's because your hands are itchy. You're afraid to admit that.

qa.q: 「喫魚喫中間」——你捨得放棄魚頭魚尾嗎？還是總想把整條魚都喫完？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 反轉做多方案貫穿順勢而為的思維，趨勢確認多頭才入市，追求波段利潤（喫魚喫中間），一個週期至少有3次操作機會，投入資金至少要佔總資金的70%以上。想喫整條魚的人，最後常常連魚身都喫不到——貪婪的代價，是連確定的利潤都失去。你怕承認，自己就是那個貪心的人。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 The reversal-to-long strategy follows the trend-thinking mindset: you only enter when the trend confirms bullish, aiming for swing profits (eating the middle of the fish). At least 3 operation chances per cycle, and you should put at least 70% of your capital in. People who want to eat the whole fish often end up missing even the middle—greed costs you the certain profits. You're afraid to admit you're that greedy person.

qa.q: 5%和2.5%的資金上限——你遵守過嗎？還是覺得「就這一次，多放點」？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 兩者都是高風險短線操作：單邊追漲如做第三浪，可能站在最高點，須有壯士斷腕勇氣，資金不超過總資金5%；超跌反彈是刀口上舔血，資金不超過總資金2.5%。上限不是建議，是保命線——你破一次線，等於把「試錯」升級成「賭命」。你怕承認，自己總說就這一次。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 Both are high-risk short-term plays: chasing a one-way rally is like riding the third wave—you could end up at the very top, so you need the courage to cut losses fast, and capital shouldn't exceed 5% of total. Catching oversold bounces is like licking blood off a knife—capital no more than 2.5%. The cap isn't a suggestion—it's a lifeline. Break it once, and you've upgraded "trying things out" to "betting your life." You're afraid to admit you always tell yourself it's just this once.

qa.q: 一個「機會少但最穩健」的方案——你願意等嗎？還是寧可多動幾下？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 這是短線抄底、逃頂最為穩健的方案，既注重趨勢又考慮能量的充足與否，但因過分考慮環境因素，機會相對較少，可投入資金總量的25%。機會少不是缺點，是它替你過濾了爛機會——你嫌它慢，可慢正是它穩的原因。你怕承認，自己受不了慢。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 This is the most solid plan for short-term bottom-fishing and top-catching. It weighs both trend and whether momentum is strong enough, but because it over-considers the environment, opportunities come less often. You can allocate 25% of total capital. Fewer opportunities isn't a flaw—it's the plan filtering out bad ones for you. You complain it's slow, but slowness is exactly why it's stable. You're afraid to admit you can't handle slow.

qa.q: 箱體震盪要「快進快出、自定止損」——你自問：你是果斷的人嗎？你的止損價寫下來了嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 箱體震盪適合性格果斷者快進快出，對趨勢考慮不多，須自定止損價位，資金不超過10%；短線波段兼顧趨勢與能量，操作次數減少但獲利能力與安全係數增大，資金20%。方案在挑人：果斷者做箱體、穩健者做波段——你選方案前，先問過自己的性格嗎？你怕承認，自己從沒問過。
keywords: 你的止損價寫下來了嗎
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 Box-range trading suits decisive people who move in and out quickly. It doesn't weigh the trend much, so you must set your own stop-loss, with capital not exceeding 10%. Short-term swings balance both trend and momentum—fewer trades but higher profitability and safety, with 20% capital. The plan picks its person: decisive ones do box-range, steady ones do swings—before you choose a plan, have you ever asked your own personality? You're afraid to admit you never have.

qa.q: 一個方案叫你賣、另一個叫你買——兩個信號打架時，你聽誰的？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 黃金爆破是追逐利潤最大化的超短線策略，要求快進快出，適合激烈震盪行情，捕捉超跌個股提示早介入；當它發出賣出提示而單邊追漲發出買入提示時就不能追漲。信號打架不是故障，是機制在攔你——你只看一個信號，等於把安全帶拆了上路。你怕承認，自己愛聽順耳的信號。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 Golden breakout is an ultra-short-term strategy chasing maximum profit. It demands quick in-and-out, suits violently choppy markets, catches oversold stocks and signals early entry. When it gives a sell signal while one-way chasing gives a buy signal, don't chase the rally. Conflicting signals aren't a malfunction—it's the mechanism stopping you. If you only look at one signal, that's like removing your seatbelt before driving. You're afraid to admit you only like signals that sound nice to you.

qa.q: 風險越高、投入越少——你平時是這樣配置資金的嗎？還是「越刺激越敢押」？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 風險越高、越短線的方案資金上限越嚴格（5%、2.5%、10%等），長線穩健方案則投入大比例資金（70%、80%），體現全書安全賺錢、控制風險的核心理念。資金管理不是保守，是讓你在最刺激的時候死得最慢——你反著來，刺激的時候押最多，市場最喜歡你這種人。你怕承認，自己興奮就手癢。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 The higher the risk and the shorter the timeframe, the stricter the capital limit (5%, 2.5%, 10%, etc.). For long-term steady plans, we put in a large chunk of capital (70%, 80%)—that reflects the core philosophy of making money safely and controlling risk. Capital management isn't being conservative—it's what keeps you dying the slowest when things get most exciting. If you do it backwards and bet the most when it's hottest, the market loves people like you. You're afraid to admit—when you get excited, your hands start itching.

qa.q: 「賣掉的都是好股票」——你也有這種痛嗎？你知道痛在哪裡嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 投資歷史越長體會越深的不是買不到好股票，而是被賣掉的都是好股票；虧錢的根源在於憑感覺操作、心口不一，應用固定簡單的方法長期堅持，直至賺錢。痛不在賣飛，在於你明明知道「心口不一」，卻從沒打算改——你賣的不是股票，是紀律。你怕承認，賣飛是因為坐不住。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 The longer your investing history, the deeper you realize: it's not that you can't find good stocks—it's that the ones you sold were the good ones. The root of losing money is trading on feelings and not walking your talk. You should stick to a fixed, simple method over the long haul until it makes you money. The pain isn't in selling too early—it's that you know you're 'not walking your talk' and you've never actually planned to change. You're not selling stocks—you're selling discipline. You're afraid to admit—you sell early because you can't sit still.

qa.q: 你賣完就漲、買完就跌——你覺得是運氣差，還是別的原因？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 因為缺乏對股票市場的瞭解與有效分析工具，操作全憑感覺和想當然，從未認真分析過股票；即使分析了，行為也與思維不統一，心口不一是盈利最大的障礙。賣完就漲不是市場針對你，是你的賣點從來不是分析出來的，是情緒逼出來的——情緒總在最低點附近喊「快跑」。你怕承認，那一刻是怕在喊。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 It's because you lack understanding of the stock market and effective analysis tools. You trade entirely on feelings and assumptions, never seriously analyzing stocks. Even when you do analyze, your actions don't match your thinking. Not walking your talk is the biggest obstacle to profit. When it rises right after you sell, it's not the market targeting you—it's that your sell point was never analyzed; it was forced out by emotion. Emotion always screams 'run' near the bottom. You're afraid to admit—that moment, it was fear doing the screaming.

qa.q: 日線管買賣點、周線管持股持幣——你讓這兩個「官員」各司其職了嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 用日線把握買賣點、尋找最好的介入價位，用周線跟蹤作為持股的依據，盡可能做到利潤最大化；當用日線無法決定持股還是持幣時，就用周線分析來解決問題。你讓日線一個人幹兩個人的活，等於讓短線波動決定長線去留——不亂纔怪。你怕承認，自己常讓日線做決定。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 Use the daily chart to nail buy and sell points and find the best entry price. Use the weekly chart to track and hold positions, maximizing profits. When the daily chart can't decide whether to hold or stay in cash, use the weekly chart to solve the problem. You're making the daily chart do two people's jobs—which is basically letting short-term noise decide long-term direction. No wonder it's a mess. You're afraid to admit—you often let the daily chart make the call.

qa.q: 週期太短易錯、太長太慢——你找過那個「事半功倍」的平衡點嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 分析週期越短敏感程度越高但失誤率也高，週期越長穩定性越好但較為滯後；通過觀察發現用好周線分析週期可以起到事半功倍的效果，兼顧穩定與敏感。你嫌短線太吵、長線太悶，於是乾脆不設週期——沒有周期的人，永遠被價格牽著走。你怕承認，自己從沒好好選過週期。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 The shorter the analysis timeframe, the more sensitive but also the higher the error rate. The longer the timeframe, the more stable but also more lagging. Through observation, you'll find that using the weekly chart well can get twice the result with half the effort—it balances stability and sensitivity. You find short-term too noisy and long-term too boring, so you just skip having a timeframe entirely—and without a timeframe, you'll always be dragged around by price. You're afraid to admit—you never seriously chose a timeframe.

qa.q: 周線紅色、滿倉持股——你上一次「滿倉拿住不動」堅持了多久？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 紅色表示多頭趨勢，應當堅持持倉，滿倉等候利潤最大化，不因短線波動而動搖。滿倉不難，難的是「不因短線波動而動搖」——你動搖一次，就等於把周線的判斷交給日線的情緒。你怕承認，動搖是怕利潤回吐。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 Red means an uptrend. You should hold your position firmly, stay fully invested to maximize profits, and not be shaken by short-term fluctuations. Being fully invested isn't hard—what's hard is 'not being shaken by short-term fluctuations.' You get shaken once, and you've handed weekly-chart judgment over to daily-chart emotion. You're afraid to admit—being shaken is the fear of giving back profits.

qa.q: 周線綠色、清倉持幣——你能空倉多久？空倉時你在想什麼？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 綠色表示空頭趨勢，應當堅持空倉，清倉持幣，耐心等待機會出現。空倉不是無所事事，是紀律在替你看守資金——你空倉三天就手癢，是因為你把「持有現金」誤當成「錯過機會」。你怕承認，自己空倉就手癢。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 Green means a downtrend. You should stay out of the market, keep everything in cash, and wait patiently for opportunities to appear. Being in cash isn't idleness—it's discipline watching over your money. If you get itchy after three days in cash, it's because you mistake 'holding cash' for 'missing opportunities.' You're afraid to admit—you get itchy when you're in cash.

qa.q: 黃色橫盤、半倉觀望——「一半資金一半股票」，你守得住這個「一半」嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 黃色表示橫盤觀望趨勢，應當堅持半倉操作，一半資金一半股票，耐心等候智能趨勢線進一步提示再作決定。半倉是對不確定性的尊重——你嫌半倉不過癮，可橫盤期滿倉的風險，往往比「不過癮」貴得多。你怕承認，自己貪那點滿倉的過癮。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 Yellow means a sideways, wait-and-see trend. You should stay half in—half cash, half stock—and patiently wait for the smart trend line to give further signals before deciding. Half position is respect for uncertainty. You think half isn't exciting enough, but the risk of being fully invested during a sideways phase usually costs way more than 'not exciting.' You're afraid to admit—you crave that thrill of being fully in.

qa.q: 周線金叉、趨勢線紅色——「行情再次拉昇的開始」，你敢信嗎？還是覺得「已經漲不少了」？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 金叉表示多頭趨勢將再次啟動：若趨勢線為紅色，表示行情再次拉昇的開始；若趨勢線為綠色，則表示一個不小級別的反彈將要展開。你覺得「漲不少了」，是因為你用過去的漲幅衡量未來的空間——而趨勢啟動的信號，從來不看已經漲了多少。你怕承認，自己總拿過去量未來。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 A golden cross means the uptrend is about to kick off again: if the trend line is red, that's the start of another push higher; if it's green, a pretty decent-sized rebound is about to unfold. You think it's 'already risen a lot' because you're measuring future potential with past gains—but trend-start signals never look at how much has already been gained. You're afraid to admit that you're always using the past to size up the future.

qa.q: 周線死叉、趨勢線綠色——「還有一段跌幅」，你聽到的是警告，還是抄底機會？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 死叉表示空頭趨勢將再次啟動：若趨勢線為綠色，表示還有一段時間的跌幅；若趨勢線為紅色，表示價格將展開盤整，不下跌也不會漲到哪兒去。你聽到「還有跌幅」就想抄底，是因為你總想買在最低——可最低點是事後才知道的，死叉只告訴你「還沒到底」。你怕承認，自己總想抄在最低。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 A death cross means the downtrend is about to kick off again: if the trend line is green, there's still more downside to come; if it's red, prices will enter a consolidation phase—not dropping much, but not going anywhere either. When you hear 'more downside ahead' and want to catch the falling knife, it's because you always want to buy at the very bottom—but the bottom is only known in hindsight. A death cross just tells you 'it's not bottomed out yet.' You're afraid to admit that you're always trying to catch the lowest point.

qa.q: 日線轉綠、你很迷茫——那時你問過周線嗎？還是直接憑迷茫做了決定？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 周線只是用來跟蹤，並不是買賣的依據。例如16元買入的股票橫盤一個月、日線轉綠時很迷茫，但若周線趨勢線仍紅且隨機指標再度金叉，就應繼續持有，說明它還有潛力。迷茫不是做決定的理由，是去問更大週期的信號——你憑迷茫下單，等於讓情緒當你的分析師。你怕承認，自己常讓心情當分析師。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 The weekly chart is just there for tracking, not a buy/sell trigger. For example, if a stock you bought at 16 yuan goes sideways for a month and the daily line turns green, it might feel confusing—but if the weekly trend line is still red and the stochastic indicator golden-crosses again, you should keep holding, because it means there's still potential. Being confused is not a reason to make a decision; it's a sign to go check the bigger timeframe—if you place orders based on confusion, you're letting your emotions be your analyst. You're afraid to admit that you often let your mood call the shots.

qa.q: 「持股還是持幣」——這種戰略級問題，你通常怎麼決定？憑感覺，還是憑指標？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 主張用傳統技術指標解決，主要三種方法：移動平均線（周線）、EXPMA指標、成交量移動平均線，以趨勢方向決定持股或持幣，並配合其他指標確認買賣信號。戰略問題最忌諱憑感覺——感覺是情緒的翻譯官，而情緒不懂趨勢。你怕承認，自己決定倉位靠的是感覺。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 My approach is to use traditional technical indicators, mainly three methods: moving averages (weekly), EXPMA, and volume moving averages. Use the trend direction to decide whether to hold shares or cash, and confirm buy/sell signals with other indicators. Strategic decisions should never rely on gut feeling—feelings are the translator of emotions, and emotions don't understand trends. You're afraid to admit that your position sizing is based on how you feel.

qa.q: 10周線和30周線——你算過自己持倉股票的多空排列嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 在周線分析週期設置一條10周平均線與一條30周平均線；二者處多頭排列就堅持持股，若處空頭排列則堅持持幣，以中期趨勢決定倉位方向。兩條線的排列，是中期趨勢的「身份證」——你從不看它，等於跟一個沒有身份證的人簽合同。你怕承認，自己從沒核對過那兩條線。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 On the weekly chart, set up a 10-week moving average and a 30-week moving average. If they're in a bullish alignment, stay in the stock; if they're in a bearish alignment, stay in cash. Let the medium-term trend decide your position direction. The alignment of those two lines is like the ID card of the medium-term trend—you've never looked at it, which is like signing a contract with someone who has no ID. You're afraid to admit you've never checked those two lines.

qa.q: 趨勢判斷和支撐壓力——你用EXPMA時，兩個功能都用，還是隻用了一半？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 主要採用兩個功能：第一是趨勢判斷，第二是支撐壓力；二者結合判斷當前趨勢方向與價位相對支撐壓力的位置，作為持股持幣的依據。只用趨勢不看支撐，等於知道方向卻不知道哪裡會絆倒——兩個功能合起來，纔是完整的依據。你怕承認，自己買入時不知離支撐多遠。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 I mainly use two functions: first, trend judgment; second, support and resistance. Combine them to assess the current trend direction and where the price sits relative to support/resistance, and use that as the basis for holding shares or cash. Using only trend and ignoring support is like knowing the direction but not where you might trip—combining both functions gives you the complete picture. You're afraid to admit that when you buy, you have no idea how far you are from support.

qa.q: 「多頭趨勢」或「價位在有效支撐之上」——這兩個條件，你滿足哪個纔敢持股？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 當EXPMA判斷當前趨勢處於多頭的時候持股；當EXPMA判斷目前價位處於有效支撐之上的時候持股。兩條件任一成立即可作為持股依據。條件是給你的安全網——你什麼條件都不看就持股，等於沒有安全網在高空作業。你怕承認，自己持股說不出理由。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 When EXPMA shows the current trend is bullish, hold shares; when EXPMA shows the price is above effective support, hold shares. Either condition alone is enough to justify holding. Conditions are your safety net—if you hold without checking any conditions, you're working at height without a net. You're afraid to admit that when you hold a stock, you can't even say why.

qa.q: 空頭趨勢或價位在壓力之下——你持幣，是因為條件，還是因為「跌怕了」？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 當EXPMA判斷當前趨勢處於空頭的時候持幣；當EXPMA判斷目前價位處於有效壓力位置之下的時候持幣，與持股條件正好相反。持幣的理由決定你持幣的質量——因為條件而持幣，你能安心等；因為害怕而持幣，你會在第一根陽線時衝回去。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 When EXPMA shows the current trend is bearish, hold cash; when EXPMA shows the price is below effective resistance, hold cash—the opposite of the holding conditions. The reason you hold cash determines the quality of that cash position—if you hold because of conditions, you can wait patiently; if you hold because of fear, you'll rush back in at the first green candle.

qa.q: 13日和64日成交量均線——你看過自己股票的「量」的趨勢嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 成交量的均線用日線設置，一條13日成交量均線與一條64日成交量均線，比較兩者交叉的方向以判斷趨勢多空轉換。價格會騙人，量比較誠實——你只看價不看量，等於只聽報喜不聽報憂。你怕承認，自己只聽報喜不聽報憂。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 For volume moving averages on the daily chart, use a 13-day volume MA and a 64-day volume MA, and compare the direction of their crossover to judge trend reversals. Prices can lie, but volume is more honest—if you only look at price without volume, you're only listening to the good news and ignoring the bad. You're afraid to admit that you only listen to good news and not bad news.

qa.q: 13日下穿64日——趨勢轉空，你會賣嗎？還是覺得「這次不一樣」？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 當13日下穿64日向下時表示趨勢轉為空頭，根據賣出提示賣出股票；當13日上穿64日向上時表示趨勢轉為多頭，根據其他指標的買入提示買入股票。信號給你了，執行卻要對抗「這次不一樣」的念頭——你輸給信號的每一次，都是輸給這個念頭。你怕承認，那句話是你自己說的。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 When the 13-day crosses below the 64-day, it signals a bearish turn—sell based on the sell signal. When the 13-day crosses above the 64-day, it signals a bullish turn—buy based on buy signals from other indicators. The signal is given to you, but executing it means fighting the thought of "this time it's different"—every time you lose to a signal, you're losing to that thought. You're afraid to admit that those words came from you.

qa.q: 量領先價一步——你願意「看量提前行動」嗎？還是非要等價格確認？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 因為相同參數設置的成交量均線走勢一直優先於價格移動平均線一步，能提前反映資金動向，故可作為趨勢轉換的先行信號。提前行動意味著承受「還沒確認」的不安——而市場的獎勵，恰恰只給願意提前一步的人。你怕承認，自己不敢承受提前一步的不安。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 Because volume MAs with the same parameters tend to move a step ahead of price moving averages, they can reflect capital flow direction early, making them a leading signal for trend reversals. Acting early means enduring the discomfort of "not confirmed yet"—and market rewards, precisely, only go to those willing to step ahead. You're afraid to admit that you can't bear the discomfort of stepping ahead.

qa.q: 你習慣用某個指標，是因為它「簡單好用」，還是因為你只會這一個？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 因為它較為方便、用起來簡單，所以作者習慣用它；但傳統技術指標同樣有理想技巧解決持股持幣問題，本章所述即拋磚引玉之談。習慣不是忠誠——你只會一個指標，不等於它最適合你，只說明你懶得學第二個。你怕承認，自己懶得學第二個。
keywords: 還是因為你只會這一個
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 Because it's convenient and simple to use, the author is used to it; but traditional technical indicators also have solid techniques to solve the holding-vs-cash problem—what's described here is just a starting point for discussion. Habit isn't loyalty—just because you only know one indicator doesn't mean it's the best fit for you, it just means you're too lazy to learn a second one. You're afraid to admit that you're too lazy to learn a second one.

qa.q: 你買股票，是不是總希望「買了就漲、賣了就跌」？——這個念頭害過你幾次？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 不追求買入就漲、賣出就跌的完美點位，過分追求完美容易使心理失衡，心理失衡下做什麼都不成功；應樹立合理目標、對投資行為提出恰當要求，理念平和並在技術上做補救。「買了就漲」的期待，讓你在買入後一刻不停地盯盤——而盯盤，是拿不住股票的開始。你怕承認，盯盤是怕錯過。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 Don't chase the perfect entry or exit—overly pursuing perfection easily unbalances your mindset, and with an unbalanced mindset, nothing you do succeeds. You should set reasonable goals, hold your investment actions to appropriate standards, keep a calm philosophy, and make technical backups. The expectation of "it'll go up right after I buy" keeps you glued to the screen the moment you buy—and staring at the screen is the beginning of not being able to hold your stock. You're afraid to admit that staring at the screen is about fearing you'll miss out.

qa.q: 你總想買在最低、賣在最高——你知道這個「理想」正在怎麼傷害你嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 大多數人都希望買在最低價、賣在最高價，這種理想化的想法導致投資人在買賣時發生困擾；過分追求完美會讓心理失衡，而心理失衡的狀態下做什麼事情都不會成功。追求完美的人，把每一次「不完美」都變成對自己的審判——審判久了，手就軟了。你怕承認，審判久了手就軟。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 Most people want to buy at the lowest price and sell at the highest—this idealistic thinking causes confusion when trading. Over-pursuing perfection will unbalance your psychology, and in an unbalanced state, nothing you do will succeed. People who chase perfection turn every "imperfection" into a judgment against themselves—judge yourself too long, and your hands go soft. You're afraid to admit that judging too long makes your hands soft.

qa.q: 基本面評估、周線看大趨勢、日線看現狀——這三步，你買股票時走過幾步？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 第一步做基本面評估；第二步用周線分析週期對大趨勢做出評估；第三步用日線的各項技術指標對當前狀態做出評估。三步得出的結論只是輪廓概念，只能落在某個價位區間。你跳過前兩步直接看日線，等於不問「這是什麼公司、大勢如何」就問「今天能不能買」。你怕承認，自己總跳過前兩步。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 Step one: do a fundamental assessment. Step two: use the weekly chart cycle to assess the bigger trend. Step three: use daily technical indicators to assess the current state. The conclusions from these three steps are just a rough outline, and can only land within a certain price range. If you skip the first two steps and go straight to the daily chart, that's like asking "can I buy today?" without asking "what kind of company is this, and what's the overall market doing?" You're afraid to admit that you always skip the first two steps.

qa.q: 分析只能得出「價位區間」，給不出「精確點位」——你能接受這種不完美嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 分析判斷只能得出價位區間，如中國銀行股5元左右可大膽介入，4元附近買入佔便宜、6元左右買入喫虧；具體買價無法由大方向分析精確到點位，需靠戰術手段解決。你要精確點位，是因為你想要「零風險」的錯覺——可投資裡，區間纔是真實，點位只是幻覺。你怕承認，自己要的是零風險的錯覺。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 Analysis and judgment can only give you a price range—for example, Chinese bank stocks around 5 yuan are worth buying boldly, buying near 4 yuan is a bargain, and buying around 6 yuan is overpaying. The exact buy price can't be pinpointed from broad trend analysis; it needs tactical methods to handle. You want precise points because you want the illusion of "zero risk"—but in investing, the range is what's real, and the point is just an illusion. You're afraid to admit that what you want is the illusion of zero risk.

qa.q: 「買不買」和「多少錢買」——你分得清自己糾結的是哪一個嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 買還是不買某隻股票是戰略問題，用多少價位買入是戰術問題；為有效解決戰術問題，作者在實戰中發現使用60分鐘的分析週期能很好地解決買賣價格的戰術問題。你常常用戰術的糾結逃避戰略的決定——「再想想多少錢買」是「其實我不想買」的體面說法。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 Whether to buy or not buy a stock is a strategic question; the price to buy at is a tactical question. To effectively solve the tactical question, the author found in practice that using a 60-minute analysis cycle works great for the buy/sell price issue. You often use tactical hesitation to avoid strategic decisions—'let me think more about the price' is just a polite way of saying 'I don't really want to buy.'

qa.q: 趨勢神經線＋隨機指標——你知道為什麼偏偏是這兩個組合嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 選擇颶風智能趨勢神經線與哈瑞隨機指標兩項指標組合，用60分鐘分析週期解決買賣價格的戰術問題。一個管方向、一個管節奏，缺一個就會失衡——你只會用其中一個，等於只用一隻腳走路。你怕承認，自己一直在單腿跳。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 Combine the Hurricane Smart Trend Neural Line and the Harry Stochastic Indicator, and use the 60-minute analysis cycle to handle the tactical issue of buy/sell price. One handles direction, the other handles rhythm—if one's missing, you lose your balance. If you only use one, it's like walking with one foot. You're afraid to admit you've been hopping on one leg all along.

qa.q: 神經線紅色＋隨機金叉——信號出現時，你的手是聽信號的，還是聽「再等等」的？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 颶風智能趨勢神經線為紅色，同時哈瑞隨機指標出現金叉，即為買入信號。方法看似簡單，但在實戰中效果非常好，可使買入價格更理想。簡單的方法最大的敵人是「太簡單了不敢相信」——你加了一堆「自己的判斷」之後，簡單信號就失效了。你怕承認，自己信不過簡單。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 When the Hurricane Smart Trend Neural Line is red and the Harry Stochastic Indicator shows a golden cross, that's a buy signal. The method looks simple, but it works really well in practice and gets you a better buy price. The biggest enemy of a simple method is 'too simple to believe'—once you pile on a bunch of 'your own judgments,' the simple signal stops working. You're afraid to admit you don't trust simplicity.

qa.q: 神經線綠色＋隨機死叉——賣出信號出現時，你捨得嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 颶風智能趨勢神經線為綠色，同時哈瑞隨機指標出現死叉，即為賣出信號。在選股過程完成、確定好要買賣的股票後使用，可抓住更佳的價位。捨不得賣，是因為你把「賣出」當成「認輸」——可賣出不是認輸，是執行規則。你怕承認，自己把賣出當認輸。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 When the Hurricane Smart Trend Neural Line is green and the Harry Stochastic Indicator shows a death cross, that's a sell signal. Use this after you've completed the stock selection process and confirmed which stock to trade—it helps you catch a better price. You can't bear to sell because you treat 'selling' as 'admitting defeat'—but selling isn't admitting defeat, it's executing the rules. You're afraid to admit you see selling as surrendering.

qa.q: 好的買賣價能「平衡心態、增加自信」——你體驗過「交易後更自信」的感覺嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 不僅能抓住最佳價位，而且這個買賣價格能平衡心態，讓你更有信心相信自己是優秀的，從而獲得更多自信；自信是成功的基礎，兩者相輔相成。你沒體驗過，是因為你從沒給自己一個「好價位」——總在恐慌或衝動中下單的人，交易完只有疲憊，沒有自信。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 Not only does it help you catch the best price, this buy/sell price also balances your mindset, making you more confident in your own excellence and giving you more self-confidence. Confidence is the foundation of success—the two reinforce each other. You've never experienced that because you've never given yourself a 'good price'—people who always place orders in panic or impulse end up exhausted after trading, not confident.

qa.q: 60分鐘週期只配「已確定買賣」的股票用——你把它拿來選股過嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 前提是你已用各種方法確定要買賣該股票，才能用60分鐘分析週期尋找合理的買賣點；這個週期不能作為選股條件，這一點無論如何要銘記。工具用對地方是利器，用錯地方是兇器——你拿60分鐘選股，等於拿手術刀切麵包，切得再快也切不對。你怕承認，自己常拿手術刀切麵包。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 The premise is that you've already used various methods to confirm you want to trade that stock—only then can you use the 60-minute analysis cycle to find a reasonable buy/sell point. This cycle can't be used for stock selection, and you must remember that no matter what. A tool used properly is a weapon; used improperly, it's a dangerous instrument. Using a 60-minute chart to pick stocks is like using a scalpel to cut bread—no matter how fast you cut, it won't cut right. You're afraid to admit you often use a scalpel for bread.

qa.q: BIAS＋BOLL、EXPMA＋KDJ——你用過「組合拳」嗎？還是永遠只會一招？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 主張用傳統技術指標組合來解決買賣點，習慣以日線的短線買賣方案實施，具體包括BIAS組合BOLL、EXPMA組合KDJ兩套買賣法。單一指標會誤報，組合是讓兩個信號互相把關——你只會一招，等於讓一個人既當球員又當裁判。你怕承認，自己只會一招。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 We advocate using traditional technical indicator combos to solve buy/sell points, and we usually implement it with a daily-line short-term trading plan. Specifically, there are two methods: BIAS combined with BOLL, and EXPMA combined with KDJ. A single indicator gives false signals; combining them lets two signals check each other—if you only know one move, it's like letting one person be both player and referee. You're afraid to admit you only know one move.

qa.q: 你拿短線方法「選股」過嗎？——你知道這是在本末倒置嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 前提是已經用綜合的方法確定了要買的股票；否則短線買入股票的方案並不是選股的方法，不能當作選股工具使用。短線信號是用來「執行」的，不是用來「選股」的——你拿它選股，等於讓執行官兼任決策者，權力越大，錯得越遠。你怕承認，自己常拿執行官當決策者。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 The premise is that you've already used comprehensive methods to decide which stock to buy; otherwise, a short-term buy plan isn't a stock-picking method and can't be used as a stock-picking tool. Short-term signals are meant for 'execution,' not 'stock selection'—if you use them to pick stocks, it's like letting the executor also be the decision-maker. The more power, the further you go astray. You're afraid to admit you often treat the executor as the decision-maker.

qa.q: BOLL向上、價格跌破下軌、6日BIAS負值超5——這種「超跌」你敢買嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 當BOLL向上、價格跌破BOLL下軌或者中軌、6日BIAS負值超過5時買入，即乖離過大且軌道仍向上時視為低吸機會。超跌買入考驗的不是技術，是你敢不敢在「看起來還要跌」的時候出手——不敢的人，永遠在等「更確定」，而更確定的時候已經不是低吸了。你怕承認，自己不敢在超跌時出手。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 When BOLL is pointing up and price breaks below the lower band or middle band, and the 6-day BIAS negative value exceeds 5, that's when you buy. In other words, when the deviation is too big but the channel is still rising, it's a dip-buying opportunity. Buying oversold conditions isn't about skill—it's about whether you dare to act when it 'looks like it'll drop more.' Those who don't dare are forever waiting for 'more confirmation,' and by the time it's more confirmed, it's no longer a dip. You're afraid to admit that you don't dare to act when it's oversold.

qa.q: BOLL向下、價格上穿中軌、BIAS正值超5——反彈到這，你走不走？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 當BOLL向下通道、價格向上穿破中軌或者上軌、6日BIAS正值超過5時賣出，即在下降通道反彈乖離過大時離場。下降通道裡的反彈是「逃命波」不是「機會波」——你把它當機會，是因為你太想回到成本了。你怕承認，把反彈當機會是因為不甘。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 When BOLL is in a downward channel, price breaks above the middle band or upper band, and the 6-day BIAS positive value exceeds 5, that's when you sell—meaning when a rebound in a downtrend has too much deviation, you leave. A rebound in a downtrend is a 'rescue wave,' not an 'opportunity wave'—you treat it as an opportunity because you're too eager to get back to your cost. You're afraid to admit that treating a rebound as an opportunity is because of unwillingness.

qa.q: 漲勢過急、乖離超13——你會在「漲得最爽」的時候賣出嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 當BOLL向上、價格向上穿破上軌、6日BIAS正值超過13時，可做短線賣出，屬漲勢過急的獲利了結信號。最爽的時候賣出，是最反人性的動作——可市場的規律就是：乖離越大，回歸越近；你捨不得在最爽時走，就會在回歸時加倍還回去。你怕承認，貪那口最爽的滿足。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 When BOLL is pointing up, price breaks above the upper band, and the 6-day BIAS positive value exceeds 13, you can do a short-term sell—it's a take-profit signal for an overly rapid rise. Selling at the most satisfying moment is the most counter-intuitive move—but the market's rule is: the bigger the deviation, the closer the reversion. If you can't bear to leave at the best moment, you'll pay back double when it reverts. You're afraid to admit that you crave that ultimate satisfaction.

qa.q: 趨勢多頭＋KDJ 60以下金叉——「趨勢向上、位置不高」兩個條件，你等得起嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 當EXPMA指標顯示當前趨勢為多頭、KDJ指標60以下金叉時買入，即趨勢向上配合低位金叉再進場。兩個條件同時滿足需要等——你等不起，是因為你覺得「等=錯過」；可等來的共振買點，勝率遠高於衝動買點。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 When the EXPMA indicator shows the current trend is bullish, and the KDJ forms a golden cross below 60, you buy—meaning you enter when the trend is upward and there's a low-position golden cross. Waiting for both conditions to be met takes patience—you can't wait because you think 'waiting = missing out.' But the resonance buy point you wait for has a much higher win rate than an impulsive buy point.

qa.q: 趨勢空頭＋KDJ 40以上死叉——兩個條件同時亮紅燈，你走不走？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 當EXPMA指標顯示當前趨勢為空頭、KDJ指標40以上死叉時賣出，即趨勢向下配合高位死叉則離場。兩個條件都亮紅燈還在猶豫，說明你等的不是信號，是奇蹟——而奇蹟從來不屬於不執行紀律的人。你怕承認，自己等的是奇蹟。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 When the EXPMA indicator shows the current trend is bearish, and the KDJ forms a death cross above 40, you sell—meaning when the trend is downward and there's a high-position death cross, you leave. If both conditions are flashing red and you're still hesitating, it means you're not waiting for a signal—you're waiting for a miracle. And miracles never belong to those who don't follow discipline. You're afraid to admit that what you're waiting for is a miracle.

qa.q: 你分得清「選股」和「執行」嗎？——你上次是不是把執行當成了選股？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 因為短線買入只是確定標的之後的執行環節，若未經綜合方法選股就倉促短線買入，會混淆選股與交易，導致盲目進場。選股是「買什麼」，執行是「怎麼買」——你把兩者混在一起，等於沒想清楚買什麼就急著問怎麼買。你怕承認，自己常先買了再說。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 Because short-term buying is just the execution step after you've confirmed the target. If you rush into a short-term buy without a combined method for stock selection, you'll confuse stock selection with trading, leading to blind entries. Stock selection is 'what to buy,' execution is 'how to buy'—if you mix them up, it's like asking how to buy before you've even figured out what to buy. You're afraid to admit that you often just buy first and think later.

qa.q: 價格、軌道、乖離、趨勢、金叉死叉——這些信號一致時，你敢信嗎？還是總覺得「太巧了」？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 BIAS組合BOLL以價格與軌道位置配合乖離率確認超買超賣；EXPMA組合KDJ以趨勢方向配合金叉死叉，兩者都要求趨勢與指標方向一致。共振不是巧合，是不同角度的信號指向同一結論——你覺得「太巧」，是因為你習慣了單一信號的含糊。你怕承認，自己習慣了含糊。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 BIAS combined with BOLL uses price and band position along with the deviation rate to confirm overbought/oversold; EXPMA combined with KDJ uses trend direction along with golden/death crosses. Both require the trend and indicator direction to align. Resonance isn't coincidence—it's different angles pointing to the same conclusion. You think it's 'too coincidental' because you're used to the vagueness of a single signal. You're afraid to admit that you're used to vagueness.

qa.q: 你交易的目的是「利益最大化」——但你上一次先想的是「資金安全」嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 交易目的是利益最大化；要達此目的，首先必須保證資金安全，否則利益最大化只是一種美好的願望。安全是盈利的前提，本金受損會摧毀後續盈利的基礎。你只盯著「最大化」，把「安全」當成保守——可沒有安全，最大化只是帳戶歸零前的幻想。你怕承認，自己從沒先想安全。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 The goal of trading is maximizing profit. To achieve that, you must first ensure capital safety—otherwise, maximizing profit is just a wishful thought. Safety is the prerequisite for profitability; losing principal destroys the foundation for future gains. You only stare at 'maximizing' and treat 'safety' as conservative—but without safety, 'maximizing' is just a fantasy before your account hits zero. You're afraid to admit that you've never thought about safety first.

qa.q: 虧損要止損、盈利要耐心——這兩條，你哪一條做得最差？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 一旦虧損必須嚴格執行止損；一旦盈利則要有耐心，堅持不要隨意平倉。如此才能保證資金安全並使盈利最大化，即小虧大賺、截斷虧損、讓利潤奔跑。多數人正好相反：虧損時死扛（捨不得止損），盈利時快跑（拿不住利潤）——你虧的每一筆，都是這兩條紀律各錯一半的結果。你怕承認，自己虧時死扛、賺時快跑。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 Once you're in a loss, you must strictly execute your stop-loss. Once you're in profit, be patient and don't close casually. That's how you protect your capital and maximize gains—small losses, big wins, cut losses short, and let profits run. Most people do the opposite: they hold on for dear life when they're losing (can't bear to stop out) and run away fast when they're winning (can't hold onto profits). Every losing trade you take is the result of getting both of these rules half wrong. You're afraid to admit it: you hold when you lose, and you bail when you win.

qa.q: 十次交易可以錯七次，但一次虧損不能超20%——你設過這個「20%紅線」嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 股票交易不追求成功率，而追求盈利率，可以容忍10次交易中有7次失敗，但堅決不能容忍1次失敗交易虧損超過20%。以單次虧損上限換整體盈利，是紀律的核心。你追求「每單都對」，於是從不設紅線——不設紅線的人，一次失誤就能吞掉十次成功。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 Stock trading isn't about win rate, it's about profitability. You can tolerate 7 losses out of 10 trades, but you absolutely cannot tolerate a single losing trade down more than 20%. Swapping a per-trade loss limit for overall profit is the core of discipline. You chase 'every trade has to be right,' so you never set a red line—and anyone who doesn't set a red line can have one mistake swallow up ten successes.

qa.q: 基本面選股＋技術面擇時＋長期重複——這三步，你缺的是哪一步？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 用基本面選擇一隻股票，用技術指標提示的買賣信號，長期堅持並簡單地重複操作，結果一定會盈利，切忌把賺錢的希望寄託在「黑馬」上。方法不缺，缺的是「長期堅持」——你總在換股票、換方法，從來沒讓一個系統跑完一個完整週期。你怕承認，自己從沒讓系統跑完一輪。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 Use fundamentals to pick a stock, use the buy/sell signals from technical indicators, and simply repeat the process over the long term—you will end up profitable. Just don't pin your hopes on a 'dark horse.' Methods aren't scarce; what's scarce is 'long-term consistency.' You're always switching stocks and methods, and you've never let a single system run through a full cycle. You're afraid to admit you've never let a system finish even one round.

qa.q: 你上一次下單的「依據」是什麼？——能寫下來嗎？還是隻有「感覺」？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 每次買賣都必須有依據而不是隨心所欲；技術指標雖不能100%保證盈利，但不用指標則100%註定發生虧損。有依據、有系統才能避免情緒化交易。你以為「感覺」也是依據——可感覺會跟著價格變，價格一動，你的依據就換了。你怕承認，自己從不把依據寫下來。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 Every buy and sell must have a basis, not be done on a whim. Technical indicators can't guarantee 100% profit, but without indicators, you're 100% guaranteed to lose. With a basis and a system, you can avoid emotional trading. You think 'feelings' count as a basis—but feelings shift with the price. The moment the price moves, your basis changes. You're afraid to admit you've never once written your basis down.

qa.q: 買進、賣出、半倉——軟體給了你三種策略，你「嚴格按提示」執行過嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 提供買進、賣出和半倉操作三種策略，會不斷發現機會和提示風險。實戰中必須選擇一隻股票長期堅持並嚴格按提示操作，切忌朝三暮四頻繁變換股票，除非基本面發生重大變故。軟體的提示不複雜，複雜的是你總想「自己補充一點」——每一次補充，都是把系統的勝率換成你的運氣。你怕承認，自己總想補充一點。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 It offers three strategies—buy, sell, and half-position—and keeps uncovering opportunities and flagging risks. In practice, you have to pick one stock, stick with it for the long haul, and strictly follow the signals. Avoid chopping and changing stocks constantly, unless there's a major change in fundamentals. The software's signals aren't complicated; what's complicated is that you always want to 'add a little something yourself.' Every time you add, you're swapping the system's win rate for your own luck. You're afraid to admit you always want to add something.

qa.q: 2萬元、48次、每次20%就能成億萬富翁——你信嗎？你等得起48次嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 因為一路滾上去的力量驚人：用2萬元做本金，交易48次每次盈利只需20%，理論上就可能成為億萬富翁（未計交易成本，僅示意複利力量）。小本金靠紀律與一路滾上去累積，急躁和沮喪會破壞對紀律的執行。你不信，是因為你要「快」；可一路滾上去的路徑恰恰是「慢」——你等不起48次，於是連第一次都做不好。你怕承認，自己等不起慢。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 Because the power of compounding is shocking: start with 20,000 yuan, trade 48 times, and with just 20% profit each time, you could become a billionaire. Small capital grows through discipline and letting it compound. Impatience and frustration wreck your ability to follow the rules. You don't believe it because you want 'fast'—but the compounding path is precisely 'slow.' You can't wait 48 trades, so you can't even get the first one right. You're afraid to admit you can't wait for slow.

qa.q: 「小虧大賺、只追求盈利率」——軟體把這理念做成了機制。你願意讓機制管住你的手嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 努力融入「小虧大賺、不追求成功率、只追求最終盈利率」的先進理念，用軟體機制幫助投資者克服人性弱點，把紀律落實為可重複執行的操作規則。你總覺得「機制不懂我的情況」——可你的「情況」，往往就是人性弱點本身；機制不是不懂你，是不慣著你。你怕承認，機制不是不懂你，是不慣著你。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 We work hard to embody the advanced philosophy of 'small losses, big gains; don't chase win rate, only chase final profitability.' The software mechanism helps investors overcome human weaknesses and turns discipline into repeatable operational rules. You always feel like 'the mechanism doesn't understand my situation'—but your 'situation' is often just human weakness itself. The mechanism isn't that it doesn't understand you; it's that it won't spoil you. You're afraid to admit: it's not that the mechanism doesn't get you—it's that it won't coddle you.

qa.q: 周線＋日線結合能「事半功倍」——你試過嗎？還是隻聽說過？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 學會把周線分析週期與日線分析週期相結合的技巧，可以起到事半功倍的效果，其結果會讓你喫驚，發現自己居然有如此高的投資水平。長短週期配合可相互驗證買賣信號。你只聽說沒試過，是因為「結合」需要先建立系統——而你還在單週期裡打轉。你怕承認，自己還在單週期打轉。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 Learn to combine weekly and daily timeframes, and you'll get twice the result with half the effort. The result will surprise you—you'll discover you actually have that high a level of investing skill. Long and short timeframes working together can cross-validate buy and sell signals. You've only heard about it but never tried it, because 'combining' requires building a system first—and you're still spinning around in a single timeframe. You're afraid to admit you're still going in circles with one timeframe.

qa.q: 你賺錢之後，還在閱讀嗎？還是賺了錢就覺得「不用學了」？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 本章主張「賺錢了也要閱讀」，即賺錢之後仍要持續閱讀學習，不可因一時獲利而停止充實自己，否則難以守住財富。賺錢是最危險的時候——它讓你以為自己已經懂了；而不讀的人，往往在下一個週期把賺的還回去。你怕承認，賺錢後自己就停了。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 This chapter is all about “keep reading even after you’ve made money.” Making profits doesn’t mean you stop learning—if you let a win convince you that you already know it all, holding onto that wealth gets a lot harder. Earning is actually the most dangerous moment—it tricks you into thinking you’ve got it figured out. And those who stop reading? They tend to give it all back in the next cycle. You’re afraid to admit it—after you made money, you stopped.

qa.q: 「不要怕」——你入場時，是帶著勇氣，還是帶著恐懼？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 是「不要怕」。寓意麪對未知與風險時要敢於行動、勇於闖蕩，不因害怕而錯失機會，這是踏出第一步的關鍵心態。你帶著恐懼入場，於是每一次波動都像審判——而「不要怕」不是魯莽，是敢於按方法行動，不是敢於亂來。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 It’s “don’t be afraid.” The idea is, when facing the unknown and risk, you gotta dare to act and go for it. Don’t let fear make you miss the chance—that mindset is what gets you to take that first step. You walked in carrying fear, so every little fluctuation felt like a judgment. But “don’t be afraid” isn’t about being reckless—it’s about daring to follow your method, not daring to go wild.

qa.q: 「不要悔」——你還在為哪一筆虧損後悔？後悔有用嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 是「不要悔」。青年30年後歸鄉時村長已過世，由村長之子轉交遺信，信中僅「不要悔」三字，告誡走過的路不必後悔。後悔是把能量倒流回無法改變的過去——你每後悔一次，就少一分力氣面對現在。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 It’s “don’t regret.” When the young man returned to his village thirty years later, the village chief had already passed away. His son handed over a letter left for him—inside, just three words: “don’t regret.” It’s a reminder that the path you walked doesn’t need to be regretted. Regret is like draining your energy backwards into a past you can’t change—every time you regret, you have a little less strength to face the present.

qa.q: 入場前「不要怕」、離場後「不要悔」——你卡在哪一個？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 對應投資全程：入場前「不要怕」，敢於按方法進場；離場後「不要悔」，對已成定局的盈虧坦然接受，並專注於未來。多數人正好相反：該進場時怕，該離場時悔——於是一輩子卡在「錯過」和「懊悔」之間。你怕承認，自己該進時怕、該走時悔。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 It maps to the whole investing journey: before you enter, “don’t be afraid”—be brave enough to follow your method and get in. After you leave, “don’t regret”—accept the wins and losses as final, and focus on what’s next. Most people do the exact opposite: they’re scared when it’s time to enter, and they regret when it’s time to leave—so they spend their whole lives stuck between “missing out” and “looking back with regret.” You’re afraid to admit it—when you should’ve entered, you were scared, and when you should’ve left, you regretted.

qa.q: 市場的漲跌已成過去——你為什麼還讓「過去」指揮「現在」的決定？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 因為市場的漲跌已成過去，後悔無助於決策；接受結果、總結經驗並持續閱讀學習，才能把教訓變成下一個機會。讓過去指揮現在，等於開車只盯後視鏡——你不是在總結，是在懲罰自己。你怕承認，自己總在懲罰自己。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 Because market ups and downs are already in the past—regret can’t help your decisions. Accepting the outcome, learning from it, and keeping up with your reading is what turns lessons into your next opportunity. Letting the past run the present is like driving while staring at the rearview mirror—you’re not reviewing, you’re punishing yourself. You’re afraid to admit it—you’re always punishing yourself.

qa.q: 你投資遇到困惑時，向誰請教？——還是隻向自己的情緒請教？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 他向村中的村長請教；村長給了他三個字的忠告「不要怕」，並講好等他回來時還有另三字相贈。青年知道向過來人請教，你卻只向自己的情緒請教——而情緒給你的答案，永遠是「快跑」或「快追」。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 He went to the village chief for advice, and the chief gave him three words: “don’t be afraid,” plus a promise that three more words would be waiting for him when he returned. He knew to ask someone who’s been through it—but you only ask your own emotions. And emotions always answer with “run” or “chase.”

qa.q: 飽經風霜後想回歸簡單——你的投資方法，是越來越簡單，還是越來越複雜？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 說明人生與投資一樣，飽經風霜之後往往想回歸簡單；而回望時最重要的不是悔恨，而是坦然面對自己的選擇與經歷。方法越複雜，往往虧得越快——因為複雜是恐懼的化妝品，簡單纔是經驗的結晶。你怕承認，複雜是怕面對簡單。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 It shows that life, like investing, often makes you want to return to simplicity after weathering storms. And when you look back, what matters most isn’t regret—it’s facing your choices and experiences with acceptance. The more complicated your method, the faster you tend to lose money—because complexity is just fear in disguise, while simplicity is the crystallization of experience. You’re afraid to admit it—complexity is your way of avoiding simplicity.

qa.q: 前幾章教方法、本章講心態——你覺得自己虧錢，缺的是方法還是心態？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 前幾章傳授具體的工具與方法，本章則以故事喻理，強調心態與紀律比技術更根本，是貫穿交易全程的信念。方法可以買、可以學，心態只能自己修——你拼命換方法，是因為換方法比修心態容易，也因為換方法不用承認自己心態有問題。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 Earlier chapters gave you specific tools and methods—this one uses a story to make a bigger point: mindset and discipline are more fundamental than technique. They’re the belief system that carries you through the entire trading journey. Methods can be bought and learned, but mindset? You can only cultivate it yourself. You keep switching methods because switching is easier than fixing your mindset—and because switching lets you avoid admitting that your mindset has issues.

qa.q: 把投資濃縮成六個字——你的投資，能濃縮成幾個字？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 體現「化繁為簡」的理念：把複雜的投資紀律濃縮為「不要怕、不要悔」六個字，人人都能記住並終身執行。能濃縮，說明你抓住了本質；濃縮不了，說明你還在細節裡打轉——而細節，是散戶最喜歡的迷宮。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 This reflects the idea of 'turning complexity into simplicity': distilling complex investment discipline into six words, 'don't fear, don't regret,' that anyone can remember and follow for life. If you can distill it, it means you've grasped the essence; if you can't, it means you're still stuck in the details—and details are the maze retail investors love most.

qa.q: 老賭客押滿36個數字，自認「必中其一」——你在股市裡，有過這種「多買幾支總會中」的想法嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 他帶36注押滿1到36共36個數字，以為開牌必中其一，因而自信必勝。但他忽略1賠35的賠率：押中只收回36注本金，押不中全輸，長期必輸。撒網式的「總會中一個」，在規則面前一文不值——你買十支股票「總有一支漲」，和押滿36個數字，是同一個幻覺。你怕承認，撒網是貪那點僥倖。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 He took 36 bets covering all numbers 1 to 36, thinking the ball would definitely land on one—so he was sure he'd win. But he ignored the 1:35 payout: if he hits, he just recovers his 36 bets as principal, if he misses, he loses everything. Over time, he's bound to lose. The 'net-casting' approach of 'one of them has to hit' is worthless against the rules—buying ten stocks thinking 'one will rise' is the same illusion as betting on all 36 numbers. You're afraid to admit that casting the net is just chasing a bit of luck.

qa.q: 「回本就走」「贏一次就收手」——你對自己說過這樣的話嗎？做到了嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 反映賭徒「贏一次就收手」的僥倖與執念，不肯見好就收、及時止損離場。把偶然結果當作必然，這種心態正是賭博與投資失敗的根本原因。「贏一次就收手」說的是收手，做的卻是繼續——你輸的每一筆，都是從「再贏一次」開始的。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 This reflects the gambler's wishful thinking and obsession with 'win once and quit'—not willing to quit while ahead or cut losses and walk away. Treating a fluke as inevitable is the root cause of gambling and investment failure. 'Win once and quit' says quit, but the action is to keep going—every loss you take starts with 'just one more win.'

qa.q: 莊家偷注，自以為神不知鬼不覺——你投資時，有沒有過這種「佔點小便宜」的念頭？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 莊家貪心，想吞下這注賭資，並以為賭客少一注不會察覺，於是決定開12：既能喫掉這注，又能留住賭客繼續下注，一舉兩得。貪小便宜的邏輯是「別人不會發現」——可市場的帳本，從不放過任何一筆貪念。你怕承認，自己也想佔點便宜。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 The dealer got greedy, wanted to swallow that bet, and thought the player wouldn't notice one missing bet, so he decided to open 12: he'd eat that bet and keep the player betting—killing two birds with one stone. The logic of grabbing small advantages is 'no one will notice'—but the market's ledger never lets any greed slip by. You're afraid to admit you also want a little piece of the pie.

qa.q: 莊家開12，結果35注全押12——你見過「貪心的代價」是什麼樣嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 莊家開12，結果臺上35個小紅布包全部押12。按1賠35需巨額賠付，賭注總額遠超莊家資本，莊家就此破產，作弊者自食其果。貪心的可怕在於：它讓你以為自己在「穩贏」，其實每一步都在把風險疊大——直到一次開牌，全部兌現。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 The dealer opened 12, and it turned out all 35 little red cloth bags on the table were betting on 12. With a 1:35 payout, the dealer owed a huge amount—the total bets far exceeded his capital, so he went broke. The cheater reaped what he sowed. The scary thing about greed is that it makes you think you're 'winning for sure,' when actually every step piles up risk—until one roll of the dice cashes it all in.

qa.q: 莊家為了「留住賭客」而開12——你有沒有為了「留住面子」而做過虧本的決定？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 說明莊家被貪念矇蔽：既想贏賭客的錢，又想留住長期「顧客」，一念貪婪決定開12，反被全部押12的賭注一舉擊垮，貪心反噬自身。為面子、為「不服輸」而繼續，是賭徒和散戶共通的死法——你上次「不認輸」的持倉，現在怎樣了？
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 It shows the dealer was blinded by greed: wanting to win the player's money and keep a long-term 'customer,' in a moment of greed he chose 12, only to be crushed by all the bets on 12. Greed backfired. Continuing for pride or refusing to admit defeat is how both gamblers and retail investors die—that position you refused to concede last time, how's it doing now?

qa.q: 老賭客的「必中」在數學上穩賠——你算過自己那些「看似穩妥」的操作，真實期望值嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 不能。36注押36個數字，賠率1賠35：押中僅收回36注本金（35倍賠付加原注），不中全虧，期望值為負，長期必輸，看似穩妥實則穩賠。「看似穩妥」是散戶最貴的錯覺——你越覺得「這樣總不會錯」，越沒算過它其實是負期望。你怕承認，自己最放心那筆從沒算過。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 No. 36 bets on 36 numbers with 1:35 odds: if you hit, you just get back your 36 bets (35x payout plus original bet), if you miss, you lose it all. Expected value is negative—over time you're guaranteed to lose. It looks safe but it's actually guaranteed to bleed. 'Looks safe' is the most expensive illusion for retail investors—the more you think 'this can't go wrong,' the less you've calculated that it's negative expectation. You're afraid to admit the position you're most confident about is the one you've never run the numbers on.

qa.q: 賭徒思維和投資紀律，差在哪裡？——你分得清自己是哪一種嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 警示貪心與僥倖：不要把「全覆蓋、必中」式的賭徒思維帶入股市，市場規則下看似保險的做法其實穩虧，必須嚴守紀律、見好就收。賭徒靠運氣下注，投資者靠紀律行動——差別不在輸贏，在於輸了之後，賭徒怪運氣，投資者查紀律。你怕承認，自己虧了也先怪運氣。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 This warns against greed and wishful thinking: don't bring that 'cover everything, must hit' gambler mindset into the stock market. Under market rules, what looks like a safe bet is actually a slow loss—you have to stick to discipline and know when to take profits. Gamblers bet on luck, investors act on discipline—the difference isn't in winning or losing, it's that after a loss, the gambler blames luck while the investor reviews discipline. You're afraid to admit that when you lose, you also blame luck first.

qa.q: 莊家本可穩贏，卻因貪念破產——你覺得自己離「莊家的貪念」有多遠？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 諷刺貪得無厭者反被貪念所害：莊家本可穩贏，卻因偷注、作弊、強行開12而傾家蕩產，說明貪婪與違規最終是搬起石頭砸自己的腳。你覺得自己不是莊家、不會那麼貪——可「再賺一點就走」和「再偷一注就好」，本是同一個念頭的兩種音量。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 It's ironic how the greedy end up getting burned by their own greed: the house was set for a steady win, but went bankrupt from sneaking bets, cheating, and forcing a 12 — greed and rule-breaking are just shooting yourself in the foot. You think you're not the house, you wouldn't be that greedy — but 'just a little more profit and I'm out' and 'just one more sneaky bet' are the same thought at two different volumes.

qa.q: 「供需決定價格」——你信，但你在交易裡用過幾次？本書說它簡單到什麼程度？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 你嘴上信「供需決定價格」，下單時卻沒用它想過一次。本章主張價格變動由供給與需求決定：供給增大價格就下降，需求增大價格就上升，這是如同日月交替一樣簡單而無須置疑的基本道理。你把它當常識背，不肯真用，是因為真用起來會擋掉你那筆衝動的單——寧可憑感覺。
keywords: 但你在交易裡用過幾次
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 You say you believe 'supply and demand sets the price,' but you've never once used it when placing an order. This chapter argues that price changes are determined by supply and demand: when supply increases, prices drop; when demand increases, prices rise. It's as simple and unquestionable as sunrise and sunset. You memorize it as common sense but refuse to really use it, because really using it would've blocked that impulsive order — you'd rather trust your feelings.

qa.q: 市場上新股發個不停，你的持股為什麼越來越不值錢？本書怎麼解釋？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 你手裡的股票越套越深，卻從沒想過市場在一直發新股。因為不斷增發新股就是市場供給增大的表現，供給增大時價格自然下降，這是適用於整個股票市場的供需原理。你懶得看發行節奏，是怕一看就發現自己的虧早被稀釋了——賴個股，比承認大環境在壓你輕鬆。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 The stocks in your hands are sinking deeper and deeper, but you've never thought about how the market keeps issuing new shares. Because the constant issuance of new shares is the market's supply increasing, and when supply increases, prices naturally fall — that's the supply-demand principle applied to the entire stock market. You can't be bothered to watch the issuance pace, because you're afraid that if you did, you'd see your losses were already diluted long ago — blaming individual stocks is easier than admitting the overall environment is squeezing you.

qa.q: 什麼情況下，市場裡的錢會「追著股票跑」？本書說的條件是什麼？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 你開始在茶餘飯後聽到親戚問「現在能不能進場」——那就是錢在找股票。書裡講的是這個條件：當有新投資人不斷加入市場，而市場上一直沒有新股發行，資金追逐有限的股票，就導致需求增大，價格上漲。你會在那個時候進場，多半不是算過供需，是怕被身邊的人落下；而人數到頂的那天，往往就是這波行情到頂的那天。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 You're starting to hear relatives ask over dinner, 'Is it time to get in now?' — that's money looking for stocks. The book describes this condition: when new investors keep flooding in while no new shares are issued, capital chases limited stocks, boosting demand and pushing prices up. When you jump in at that point, it's usually not because you calculated supply and demand — it's because you're scared of being left behind by the people around you. And the day the headcount peaks is often the day this rally peaks.

qa.q: 一隻股票沒增發，為什麼賣單還是源源不斷？本書說供給從哪來？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 你那隻賣單源源不斷，你卻只想「是不是錯殺了」。已發行的股票都分散在投資人手中，供給增大與否取決於持有者的態度：持有者普遍認為該股未來沒有潛力而爭相拋售，市場供給就增大，價格下跌。你不去問「大家為什麼逃」，是怕答案戳破你的看好——寧可相信是錯殺。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 Your sell orders just keep coming, but all you can think is 'maybe it was wrongly sold off.' Outstanding shares are scattered among investors, and whether supply increases depends on the holders' attitude: when holders generally think the stock has no future potential and rush to sell, market supply goes up and the price falls. You don't ask 'why is everyone running away?' because you're afraid the answer will pop your bullish view — you'd rather believe it was wrongly killed.

qa.q: 一隻股票為什麼會突然「買都買不到」？本書說需求從哪裡來？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 你上回搶著買那隻，心跳比思考快。投資人普遍認為某隻股票未來具有很大增值潛力，都爭相購買，而持有者又不願輕易賣出，需求就大於供給，股價自然上漲。你買前沒想過供需，是怕一冷靜就錯過——把「大家都在搶」當成理由，比自己算踏實。
keywords: 一隻股票為什麼會突然
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 Last time you rushed to buy that stock, your heart was beating faster than your head. When investors generally believe a stock has huge room to appreciate and rush to buy, while holders aren't willing to sell easily, demand exceeds supply, and the stock price naturally rises. You didn't think about supply and demand before buying because you were afraid that if you calmed down, you'd miss the chance — treating 'everyone's grabbing it' as a reason feels more solid than doing your own math.

qa.q: 如果只記一句話就能判斷股價方向，本書給的是哪句？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 你要是隻許記一句，多半會選這句。結論是：供給增大，股票價格就下降；需求增大，股票價格就上漲。作者強調問題極其簡單，看懂它、靠它就能賺錢。你記得住這句，卻指不出持倉股的供需，是貪快——把「懂了」當「會用」，下單時照舊憑感覺。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 If you're only allowed to remember one line, you'd probably pick this one. The conclusion: when supply increases, stock prices fall; when demand increases, stock prices rise. The author emphasizes the problem is extremely simple — understand it and you can make money from it. You remember this line, but you can't point out the supply and demand of your holdings. That's what being greedy for speed looks like — mistaking 'got it' for 'can use it,' and still placing orders by gut feeling.

qa.q: 你為什麼總把股市想得很複雜？本書用什麼比喻勸你回歸簡單？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 你總把股市想得高深莫測，彷彿不學一堆模型就虧得有理。因為供需與價格的關係本是常識，作者以月亮夜出、太陽日升作比，意在破除投資人把股市想得過於複雜的心態，回歸簡單本質。你愛把它想複雜，是怕承認它簡單——簡單，就等於承認自己虧在不用心。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 You always think the stock market is deep and mysterious, as if losing money is totally justified if you haven't learned a bunch of models. Because the relationship between supply, demand, and price is plain common sense — the author compares it to the moon rising at night and the sun rising in the day, to break investors' habit of overcomplicating the market and bring it back to its simple core. You love to see it as complicated because you're afraid to admit it's simple — if it's simple, that means admitting you lost because you just didn't care enough.

qa.q: 你下一次買賣前，會先觀察「誰在拋、誰在搶」嗎？本書說操作看什麼？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 你下次買賣前，別只盯那根K線。操作上應觀察市場與個股的供需變化：判斷持有者拋售意願與投資人購買熱情，供大於求時趨避，需大於供時把握上漲機會。你懶得看供需，是手癢壓過了怕——真去數誰在拋誰在搶，多半當場就該收手。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 Next time you trade, don't just stare at that one candlestick. In practice, you should observe the supply and demand dynamics of the market and the individual stock: gauge whether holders are eager to sell and whether investors are eager to buy. When supply exceeds demand, step back; when demand exceeds supply, seize the upside opportunity. If you can't be bothered to watch supply and demand, it's because your itchy trigger finger outweighs your fear — if you actually counted who's dumping and who's grabbing, you'd probably back off on the spot.

qa.q: 為什麼看一隻股票的供給，要看「持有者的心態」，而不是看發行量？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 你納悶「沒發新股，賣單哪來的」，其實就來自和你一樣的人。因為個股股份已全部分散在投資人手中，沒有新發行，供給的增減完全取決於持有者是否願意賣出，故其心態決定供給大小。你不去看持有者心態，是怕照見自己——你現在，也是那個想賣、卻還賴著的人。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 You're wondering, "No new shares issued, so where are the sell orders coming from?" They come from people just like you. Since all the shares are already scattered among investors, with no new issuance, the change in supply depends entirely on whether holders are willing to sell — so their mindset determines the size of supply. You don't look at holders' mindsets because you're afraid of seeing yourself — right now, you're also one of those who wants to sell but is still hanging on.

qa.q: 本書說「賺錢就靠它了」——你覺得這個「它」是什麼？你抓住了嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 書裡說「賺錢就靠它了」，你點點頭卻從沒試過。指靠準確把握供給與需求變化對股票價格的影響規律：在需求增大、價格上漲之前介入，避開供給增大、價格下跌的階段。你總在漲起來之後纔衝，是怕錯過的僥倖壓過了怕套——等大家都看見需求，價格早不在低位。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 The book says, "This is how you make money," and you nod along but never actually tried it. It means accurately grasping how changes in supply and demand affect stock prices: get in before demand rises and prices go up, and avoid the phase where supply increases and prices fall. You always charge in after the rally has already started — it's because the侥幸 hope of missing out outweighs your fear of being trapped — by the time everyone sees the demand, the price is no longer at the low.

qa.q: 小偷的本事不在「偷」而在「逃」——你投資的本事，練的是「偷」還是「逃」？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 主張高風險資本投資中，最重要的本領不在「偷」（賺錢），而在危急時怎麼「逃」（止損離場）；逃生與自保能力纔是贏家關鍵。你花了多少時間研究怎麼賺，就該花多少時間練習怎麼逃——只練偷不練逃的人，偷得越多，逃得越慘。你怕承認，自己只練過進、沒練過逃。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 In high-risk capital investing, the most important skill isn't "stealing" (making money), but how to "escape" (cut losses and get out) in a crisis; the ability to survive and protect yourself is the real key to winning. Spend as much time studying how to escape as you do studying how to make money — those who only practice stealing and not escaping will, the more they steal, the worse their escape. You're afraid to admit that you've only practiced going in, never practiced getting out.

qa.q: 「不要怕，也不要悔」——你入市前，先搞清遊戲規則了嗎？還是先衝了再說？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 既然參與就不要怕、也不要悔；參與之前先搞清遊戲規則，再製定與市場走勢相一致的應對策略，心態與準備缺一不可。不搞清規則就衝，等於不讀說明書就開機——你不是勇敢，是拿本金交學費。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 Since you're in the game, don't be scared and don't regret; before jumping in, understand the rules of the game, then formulate a strategy that aligns with market trends. Mindset and preparation are both essential.
