It does look a bit laggy on smaller timeframes, but on bigger mid-to-long-term moves, it rarely misses the boat, so it doesn't affect that style of trading. The lag is only a flaw in little ripples—in big tides, it's actually a strength: stable, so you don't get shaken off by minor fluctuations. The reason the lag hurts you is usually because you're using a mid-to-long-term ruler to do short-term work. You're afraid to admit you used the wrong tool for the job.

qa.q: 「看起來簡單」和「實用性非常高」為什麼能同時成立？矛盾在哪？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 不矛盾，矛盾的是你的執行。因為規則只有快慢線交叉配合價線支撐壓力兩點，看似簡單，但大行情很難被遺漏，實戰中用得久會發現奇妙無比。簡單的規則容易被輕視——「就這？」於是你擅自加料、擅自跳過、擅自「改良」，最後把一套好方法改得面目全非；不是方法簡單，是你不甘於簡單。
qa.a_en: Heyyy~ 😊 It's not contradictory—what's contradictory is your execution. Because the rule is just two things: fast/slow line crossovers combined with price line support/resistance. Sounds simple, but big moves rarely slip through, and the longer you use it in live trading, the more magical it feels. Simple rules get easily underestimated—"That's it?"—so you add extra stuff, skip steps, and "improve" it until it's a mess. The method isn't too simple; you just can't handle simplicity.

qa.q: 買點賣點出現要「迅速行動」——「迅速」兩個字，在跟你的什麼習慣作對？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 跟「猶豫」作對，也跟「頻繁」作對。買點賣點出現時要迅速買入賣出，不猶豫、不頻繁操作，用中長線方法耐心持盈，才能安全賺錢。這是一組矛盾的紀律：該動時要快，不該動時要忍——多數人剛好反過來：該買時猶豫錯過，買完後天天手癢亂動。迅速與耐心，缺一個都不行。你是哪一個？
keywords: 在跟你的什麼習慣作對
qa.a_en: Heyyy~ 😊 You're fighting "hesitation" and also fighting "over-trading." When buy/sell signals appear, act quickly—buy or sell without hesitating, don't overtrade, and hold patiently with a mid-to-long-term approach to let profits run safely. It's a pair of contradictory disciplines: move fast when you should, hold back when you shouldn't. Most people do exactly the opposite: hesitate at entries and miss, then fidget and overtrade afterwards. Speed and patience—missing either one won't work. Which one are you?

qa.q: 作者用「軍人、狼」來考你——這兩個比喻，分別在測你的什麼？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 軍人測「服從」，狼測「狠心」。須有軍人服從紀律的素質、果斷剛毅的性格，以及如狼被夾住腿時毫不猶豫咬斷自己腿逃生般的殘忍決心，三問皆肯定才具備短線交易資格。紀律讓你在該動時動手，狠心讓你在該斷時斷腿——兩個都缺的人做短線，等於沒有煞車也沒有方向盤就上路。
qa.a_en: Heyyy~ 😊 Soldiers are tested on "obedience," wolves on "ruthlessness." You need a soldier's discipline, a decisive and tough personality, and the brutal resolve of a wolf that will bite off its own trapped leg without hesitation to escape. If all three answers are yes, then and only then do you qualify for short-term trading. Discipline makes you strike when you should; ruthlessness makes you cut when you should. Someone lacking both who trades short-term is like driving with no brakes and no steering wheel.

qa.q: 短線方法那麼多，為什麼偏偏是「中長期的BOLL＋短線的BIAS」？這組合妙在哪？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 妙在「一個定軌道，一個量偏差」。BOLL與BIAS組合分析。因BOLL是中長期綜合指標，反映股價運行軌跡與波動極限；BIAS是短線指標，判斷股價偏離度以提醒短期風險與機會，兩者結合能各自發揮最大優勢。做短線最怕「只見樹木不見森林」——BOLL是森林的方向，BIAS是樹木的偏離；一個管「在哪裡」，一個管「跑多遠」。你兩樣都帶了嗎？
qa.a_en: Heyyy~ 😊 The magic is in "one sets the track, the other measures the deviation." That's the combined analysis of BOLL and BIAS. Because BOLL is a mid-to-long-term composite indicator—it reflects the stock's movement path and volatility limits. BIAS is a short-term indicator that measures how far price has deviated, reminding you of short-term risks and opportunities. Together, they play to each other's strengths. In short-term trading, the worst fear is "missing the forest for the trees"—BOLL is the forest's direction, BIAS is the tree's lean. One tells you "where you are," the other tells you "how far off you've run." You got both with you?

qa.q: 「BOLL向上、價格跌破中軌或下軌、BIAS負值超過5」——為什麼「跌」反而是買點？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 因為那是「順勢裡的折扣」。當BOLL向上、價格跌破BOLL中軌或下軌，且6日BIAS負值超過5時買入；BOLL趨勢向上時買入信號要求放寬，BIAS達負值4左右即屬合理買入值。趨勢向上時，跌破軌道是「洗盤打折」不是「崩盤」——你怕的那個「跌」，正是系統叫你「買」的那個「跌」；怕跌的人，永遠買不到順勢的便宜貨。
qa.a_en: Heyyy~ 😊 Because that's "a discount within the trend." When BOLL is sloping up and price breaks below the middle or lower band, and the 6-day BIAS negative value exceeds 5, you buy. When the BOLL trend is up, the buy signal can be looser—BIAS around -4 is already a reasonable buy zone. In an uptrend, breaking below the band is "washing out at a discount," not "crashing." The "drop" you're afraid of is exactly the "drop" the system tells you to buy. People who fear drops will never catch the cheap deals that come with the trend.

qa.q: 「穿上軌＋BIAS正值超5」才賣——這個賣點，為什麼設得比你想像中「晚」？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 因為要賣在「瘋」而不是賣在「漲」。價格向上穿破BOLL上軌且6日BIAS正值超過5時賣出；BOLL趨勢向上時賣出信號要求更嚴，須BIAS正值13以上纔算超越偏離值，即賣出時機。趨勢向上時，漲破上軌常常是「強勢的開始」而不是「結束」——賣太早，等於把最肥的一段讓給別人；系統教你忍到「偏離得離譜」才收手，忍得住的人才喫得到魚身。
keywords: 為什麼設得比你想像中
qa.a_en: Heyyy~ 😊 Because you sell at "crazy," not at "up." When price breaks above the upper BOLL band and the 6-day BIAS positive value exceeds 5, you sell. When the BOLL trend is up, the sell signal needs to be stricter—BIAS above +13 counts as truly overextended, and that's your sell window. In an uptrend, breaking above the upper band is often "the start of strength," not "the end." Selling too early is giving away the fattest part of the move. The system teaches you to hold until the deviation is absurdly stretched—only those who can endure get to eat the fish body.

qa.q: 趨勢向下時，作者叫你「不要買、但要會賣」——這條不對稱的規矩，在保護你什麼？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 保護你的本金，也留住你的退路。BOLL顯示趨勢向下時最好不要參與短線買入操作；但賣出提示仍然準確，當BIAS值達到正值3左右就可以考慮賣出。下跌趨勢裡的反彈，是「逃命窗口」不是「進場機會」——買賣規則不對稱，是因為多空本來就不對稱：買錯會深套，賣早只少賺。守住這條規矩，你就不會在下跌裡越接越深。你怕自己愛接下跌的刀。
qa.a_en: Heyyy~ 😊 It protects your capital and keeps your escape route open. When BOLL shows a downtrend, it's best not to participate in short-term buying. But the sell signal stays accurate—when BIAS reaches around +3, you can consider selling. In a downtrend, a rebound is a "window to run," not a "chance to enter." Buy and sell rules are asymmetric because the market itself is: buying wrong gets you trapped deep; selling early only means making a little less. Stick to this rule, and you won't keep catching falling knives deeper and deeper. You're afraid you love catching falling knives, aren't you?

qa.q: 同樣的BIAS，為什麼「向上時要13才賣、向下時3就該賣」？標準怎麼會變？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 因為「順勢可以貪，逆勢不能貪」。BOLL的運行方向決定應用BIAS數值的大小：趨勢向上時買入信號可放寬（負4左右），賣出須更嚴格（正值13以上）；趨勢向下時買入無效，賣出信號則提前至正值3左右。順勢時，偏離一點點是正常的，讓子彈再飛一會兒；逆勢時，任何反彈都是禮物，見好就收。標準不是死的，是跟著趨勢「站隊」的。你站哪一邊？
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 It's because "you can be greedy when riding the trend, but never when going against it." The direction of BOLL decides how you apply BIAS values: when the trend is up, buy signals can be loosened (around -4), while sell signals need to be stricter (positive 13 or above); when the trend is down, buy signals are useless, and sell signals move earlier to around positive 3. When you're with the trend, a little deviation is normal—let the bullet fly a bit longer; when you're against it, any bounce is a gift—take the profit and run. Standards aren't set in stone; they follow the trend and pick a side. Which side are you on?

qa.q: 作者要你「合上書、閉上眼」先答三問，再學技巧——為什麼技巧反而排在後面？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 因為「人不行，技巧再好也沒用」。決定用短線方法前應合上書本閉眼思考三問，答案肯定與否直接決定能否參與短線交易，想好了再開始學習短線買賣技巧，強調紀律與性格比技巧更前置。技巧是工具，性格是手——手會抖的人，拿到再好的手術刀也做不了手術；作者寧可你「不學」，也不願你「學了卻用不了」。你怕承認是手會抖。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 It's because "if the person's no good, no amount of skill will save you." Before deciding to trade short-term, close the book, shut your eyes, and ask yourself three questions. Whether your answers are yes or no directly determines if you can even participate in short-term trading. Think it through before you start learning the buy/sell tricks. Discipline and character come before technique. Technique is the tool, character is the hand—if your hand shakes, even the best scalpel won't do you any good. The author would rather you "don't learn" than "learn but can't use it." You're afraid to admit your hand shakes.

qa.q: 短線選手為什麼需要一個「中長期」的指標當靠山？BOLL的優勢到底在哪？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 在「給短線畫邊界」。BOLL是中長期綜合指標，優勢在於反映股價的運行軌跡以及股價波動的極限，為短線買賣提供中期方向與上下邊界依據。短線最怕「亂竄」——沒有邊界，你就不知道跌到哪算過頭、漲到哪算瘋狂；BOLL把「極限」畫出來，短線的「進」與「出」纔有了參照系。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 This is about "drawing boundaries for short-term trading." BOLL is a mid-to-long-term comprehensive indicator. Its strength is reflecting the stock's movement path and the limits of its fluctuations, giving short-term traders a medium-term direction and upper/lower boundaries. The worst thing for short-term trading is "running around blindly"—without boundaries, you don't know how far down is too far or how far up is crazy. BOLL draws the "limits," so short-term "entries" and "exits" finally have a frame of reference.

qa.q: 有了BOLL的「軌道」，為什麼還需要BIAS的「偏離度」？它多告訴你什麼？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 多告訴你「離軌道多遠了」。BIAS是短線指標，主要功能是判斷股價的偏離度，用來提醒投資人短期風險和機會，與BOLL配合可同時把握軌跡與偏離兩種信號。軌道告訴你「極限在哪」，偏離告訴你「現在離極限還有多遠」——一個管空間，一個管進度；只看軌道不看偏離，你會以為「還早」，等偏離爆表才發現已經太晚。你怕自己總嫌太晚。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 It tells you more about "how far you are from the channel." BIAS is a short-term indicator. Its main job is to measure the deviation of the stock price, reminding investors of short-term risks and opportunities. Combined with BOLL, you get both the trajectory and the deviation signals at once. The channel tells you "where the limit is," and the deviation tells you "how far you are from that limit right now"—one handles space, the other handles progress. If you only watch the channel and ignore deviation, you'll think "there's still time," and by the time deviation blows up, you realize it's already too late. You're afraid you'll always be too late.

qa.q: 你買股票時，看的是「它值多少」，還是「它現在多少錢」？本書說價格跟著誰走？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 你買進一隻，滿腦子都是「現在多少錢」，從沒算過它值多少。價格的高低變化取決於價值的高低，價格圍繞價值而波動，價值是影響價格變動的主要因素；正如一卡車黃沙可能比不上一塊三克重的鑽石，只因鑽石價值更高。你只看價格不看價值，是貪那點數字跳動的刺激——真去算價值，怕算出來自己買貴了。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 You buy a stock, and all you can think about is "what's the price right now," but you've never calculated what it's actually worth. Price changes depend on value—price moves around value, and value is the main factor driving price. Just like a truckload of sand might not be worth a 3-gram diamond, because the diamond has much higher value. You only look at price, not value—you're hooked on the thrill of the numbers jumping. If you actually calculated the value, you'd be afraid of finding out you overpaid.

qa.q: 一卡車黃沙比不上一塊三克重的鑽石——你選股時，會不會也把「便宜」當成「黃沙」？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 你一看到「便宜股」三個字，手就癢著想撿。一卡車黃沙可能比不上一塊三克重的鑽石，原因是鑽石的價值遠高於黃沙，價格自然就高；由此可見價格變動的根本在於價值，價值是判斷價格高低的準則。你買便宜股買的是「便宜」不是價值，是貪那口撿漏的爽——真問它值多少，你答不上來。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 The moment you see the words "cheap stock," your hands itch to grab it. A truckload of sand might not match a 3-gram diamond, because the diamond's value is far higher than sand's, so naturally its price is higher. This shows the root of price movement lies in value—value is the standard for judging whether a price is high or low. What you're buying with cheap stocks is "cheapness," not value—you're craving that thrill of scoring a bargain. Ask yourself what it's worth, and you can't answer.

qa.q: 你評估一隻股票值多少錢時，會從哪幾個方面想？本書說有三個方面，你知道嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 你買一隻股票，說得出它值多少錢嗎？三種價值怕是一個都講不清。股票價值主要體現在資產淨值、未來盈利預期以及投機價值三個方面；其中資產淨值與未來盈利預期屬於投資價值的範疇，投機價值則另成一類。你答不出三種價值，是怕一認真就露了底——買的其實不是價值，是那點上漲的念想。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 When you buy a stock, can you say how much it's worth? Bet you can't explain any of the three kinds of value. Stock value mainly shows in three areas: net asset value, future earnings expectations, and speculative value. Net asset value and future earnings expectations fall under investment value, while speculative value is its own category. You can't name those three values because you're afraid that once you get serious, you'll reveal the truth—what you're actually buying isn't value, it's just the hope of a price rise.

qa.q: 你怕不怕買貴了喫虧？本書說用什麼來判斷現有價格合不合理？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 你買入前，K線看了一百遍，資產淨值從沒查過一眼。資產淨值越高，價格自然越高，反之越低；它的作用是協助判斷現有價格的高低是否合理，讓投資人避免喫虧上當。你跳過這欄，是圖省事——真查了怕算出來買貴了，寧可蒙著眼下單。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 Before you buy, you've looked at the K-line a hundred times, but you've never once checked the net asset value. The higher the net asset value, the naturally higher the price, and vice versa. Its role is to help judge whether the current price is reasonable, so investors don't get ripped off. You skip that column because you're taking the easy way out—if you actually checked, you'd be afraid of finding out you overpaid, so you'd rather place the order with your eyes closed.

qa.q: 你買股票，是買它的「現在」，還是買它的「未來」？本書說未來靠什麼判斷？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 你買股票，愛說「看好它未來」，卻講不出依據。未來盈利預期是對某隻股票未來價值的預測，判斷其未來是否還有增值潛力；它告訴投資人能否讓自己的利潤最大化。你拿「未來會好」當買的理由，是貪那個還沒發生的利潤——真要你寫出依據，多半寫不出半句。
keywords: 本書說未來靠什麼判斷
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 You buy stocks and love saying 'I'm bullish on its future,' but can't back it up with any real reasoning. Future earnings expectations are predictions about a stock's future value—whether it still has room to grow; it tells investors if they can maximize their profits. Using 'the future will be good' as your reason to buy is just chasing profits that haven't happened yet—if you actually had to write down your reasoning, you probably couldn't manage half a sentence.

qa.q: 一隻股票「現在便宜」和「未來會漲」，哪個更重要？本書說兩者是什麼關係？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 你買股票，眼裡只有「現在便宜不便宜」，未來懶得想。二者重要性幾乎一致：資產淨值判斷現有價格是否合理，避免喫虧；盈利預期判斷未來增值潛力，謀求利潤最大化，兩者同屬投資價值範疇。你只看現在，是貪那一下的安心——把未來交給想像，比認真算簡單。
keywords: 本書說兩者是什麼關係
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 You buy stocks with only one thing in your head: 'Is it cheap right now?' You can't be bothered to think about the future. Both matter almost equally: net asset value tells you whether the current price is fair so you don't get ripped off; earnings expectations tell you about future growth potential to maximize profits—both fall under investment value. Only looking at the present is just you grabbing for that moment of comfort—leaving the future to imagination is way easier than doing the hard math.

qa.q: 你知不知道市場上「大家公認的合理價位」是怎麼形成的？本書用哪個詞稱呼它？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 你心裡有個「它該值這個價」的數，誰給的你從沒想過。投機價值是指某隻股票在某一段時間範圍內的平均交易成本；它是在市場交易中產生，也是參與交易的投機者共同認可的合理價位。你那個價位多半是一廂情願，是怕承認它只是你想要的數——市場認的價，得從成交裡找。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 You've got a number in your head for 'what it should be worth,' but you've never once asked yourself where that number came from. Speculative value refers to the average transaction cost of a stock over a certain period; it's created through market trading and represents the fair price that the speculators involved collectively agree on. That price of yours is mostly wishful thinking—you're scared to admit it's just a number you want. The price the market recognizes? You have to find it in the actual trades.

qa.q: 你是「投資者」還是「投機者」？本書說不同身份，應該各看重什麼價值？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 你嘴上自稱投資者，手上的單卻全是幾天就跑。因為投機價值由市場交易產生，是投機者共同認可的合理價位，對於投機者來說，投機價值的實戰意義往往比投資價值更接近市場。你不肯認自己是投機者，是死要面子——承認了，就等於認了自己也在追漲殺跌。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 You call yourself an investor out loud, but every single order you place is gone within days. Because speculative value is born from market trading—it's the fair price that speculators collectively recognize. For speculators, the real-world significance of speculative value is often closer to the market than investment value. You won't admit you're a speculator because you're saving face—once you admit it, that's basically admitting you're also chasing peaks and selling on dips.

qa.q: 你急著想知道「怎麼算出投機價值」嗎？本書為什麼不在此處講？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 你看到「方法在後面章節」，當下就想跳去翻那頁。判斷投機價值的方法有多種多樣，本章不作探討，書中後面有專門的內容告訴讀者如何發現投機價值，屬於後續章節的內容。你急著找方法，是貪那一下能用的招——前面的道理還沒嚥下，方法到你手也用歪。
keywords: 本書為什麼不在此處講
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 You see 'the method is in the later chapters' and instantly want to flip to that page. There are many ways to assess speculative value, but this chapter doesn't dive into them—the book has dedicated content later on how to spot speculative value, which belongs in the upcoming chapters. You're rushing to find the method because you want that one quick trick you can use—but the principles before it haven't even been digested yet. Even when you get the method, you'll end up using it crooked.

qa.q: 錯過最佳買賣點，作者說「不必擔心」——這句話，先治好了你的什麼病？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 治好「錯過一次就放棄」的病。主張用KDJ結合趨勢的補救技巧，錯過最佳買賣點後仍能抓住賺錢機會，不必擔心良機白白流失，也不放棄投資生涯。很多人錯過買點後的典型反應是「算了不追了」或「追高賭一把」——前者放棄機會，後者放棄紀律；作者給你第三條路：用規則補救，而不是用情緒補救。你怕承認，亂追是怕錯過。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 Let's cure that 'missed it once, so I give up' disease. The book advocates rescue techniques that combine KDJ with trend—so even after missing the ideal buy or sell point, you can still grab profitable opportunities. No need to fear good chances slipping away, and no need to abandon your investing career. After missing a buy point, most people's typical reactions are 'forget it, not chasing now' or 'lemme gamble and chase high'—the first gives up the opportunity, the second gives up discipline. The author offers you a third path: use rules to recover, not emotions. You're afraid to admit that chasing wildly is just fear of missing out.

qa.q: 作者說KDJ「一直蒙受不白之冤」——它冤在哪？誰害的？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 冤在「被人用錯還被怪」。KDJ是短線指標中買賣效果最好的指標，但自中國股市創立以來一直蒙受不白之冤，人們對其認識一知半解，由此產生很多誤解。一知半解的人拿它單獨用、拿它在錯誤的趨勢裡用，虧了錢就怪指標——工具沒變，用的人沒變，變的只是誰來背鍋。你怕承認是自己用錯。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 The real injustice is 'being used wrong and still getting blamed.' KDJ is the most effective indicator for buy and sell signals among short-term indicators, but it's been wrongly accused ever since China's stock market was born—people's half-baked understanding has created tons of misunderstandings. People with shallow knowledge use it alone, use it in the wrong trend, and when they lose money, they blame the indicator. The tool hasn't changed, the user hasn't changed—the only thing that changes is who takes the fall. You're afraid to admit it's you who used it wrong.

qa.q: 「解決了趨勢，卻落實不了買賣」——這句話，怎麼解釋KDJ必須「搭夥」？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 因為它只會「下指令」，不會「看大局」。因為單純解決趨勢問題並不能落實具體買賣的問題，KDJ必須和趨勢指標相結合才能發揮優勢，二者有機結合可謂天衣無縫。趨勢告訴你「該不該在這個市場裡」，KDJ告訴你「這一刻動不動手」——沒有前者，你會在下跌趨勢裡被金叉騙進場；沒有後者，你知道方向卻永遠錯過時機。你怕承認自己也只看信號。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 Because it only 'gives commands,' it doesn't 'see the big picture.' Solving the trend problem alone doesn't pin down the actual buy-and-sell decisions—KDJ has to work together with trend indicators to unlock its full strength, and combining the two is a match made in heaven. The trend tells you 'should I even be in this market,' and KDJ tells you 'should I make my move right now'—without the former, you'll get fooled into entering by a golden cross in a downtrend; without the latter, you know the direction but always miss the timing. You're afraid to admit that you only look at signals too.

qa.q: 多頭裡「賣出信號忽略不計」——這條規則，最考驗你的什麼？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 考驗你「被嚇到時還記不記得規矩」。當趨勢多頭的情況下，KDJ指標發出買入信號，立即買入；發出賣出信號，可以忽略不計，只順著多頭趨勢做多。多頭裡的死叉十有八九是「嚇你下車」——你順著賣了，然後眼睜睜看它漲回去；規則說「忽略」，你卻總在那一刻選擇「相信自己的恐懼」。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 This one tests whether you still remember the rules when you're scared. In an uptrend, when the KDJ indicator gives a buy signal, buy immediately; when it gives a sell signal, you can ignore it—just keep going long with the trend. A death cross in an uptrend is nine times out of ten just trying to scare you off—if you sell, you'll watch it climb right back up. The rules say "ignore," but you always choose to "trust your fear" in that moment.

qa.q: 空頭裡「買入信號忽略不計」——這條規則，在防哪種「手癢」？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 防「搶反彈的手癢」。當趨勢空頭的情況下，KDJ指標發出賣出信號，立即賣出；發出買入信號可以忽略不計，只順著空頭趨勢逃生。空頭裡的金叉是「逃命窗」不是「進場門」——你搶進去，以為抄到底，其實是在接刀；規則早就寫好「忽略」，你卻總在那一刻覺得「這次不一樣」。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 This one's about stopping those itchy fingers that want to grab a rebound. In a downtrend, when the KDJ indicator gives a sell signal, sell immediately; when it gives a buy signal, you can ignore it—just follow the trend and escape. A golden cross in a downtrend is a "window to escape," not a "door to enter"—you jump in thinking you've caught the bottom, but really you're catching a falling knife. The rules already said "ignore," but you always think "this time it's different" in that moment.

qa.q: 同一個KDJ，為什麼「當補救很優秀、當主力就失靈」？差別在哪？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 差在「角色」。「KDJ作為錯過行情起點買賣點之後的補救措施很優秀，但單獨作為獨立的買賣指標就基本上失去了作用。」當你有趨勢當靠山，它補的是「時機」——補救角色天衣無縫；當你指望它一個人扛起全部判斷，它扛不動——就像救火隊很優秀，但你不能指望救火隊替你蓋房子。你怕承認自己用錯了角色。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 The difference is in the "role." "KDJ is excellent as a remedy after you've missed the buy/sell point at the start of a move, but on its own as an independent trading indicator, it basically loses its purpose." When you have the trend backing you up, it fills in the "timing"—that remedial role is seamless. But when you expect it to carry all the judgment by itself, it can't—like a fire brigade is great, but you can't expect the fire brigade to build your house for you. You're afraid to admit you've been using it in the wrong role.

qa.q: 「先判斷趨勢，再用KDJ」——順序為什麼不能顛倒？顛倒一次會怎樣？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 因為顛倒一次，就可能顛倒一輩子。應堅持先判斷趨勢，再考慮使用KDJ指標的買賣信號，順序不能顛倒，這是本章最核心的紀律。先看KDJ，你會「看到想看的訊號」再回頭找趨勢背書——那不是判斷，是找藉口；順序一顛倒，紀律就變成「心情好的時候才遵守」的東西。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 Because once you flip the order, you might flip it for life. You should always judge the trend first, then consider the KDJ indicator's buy/sell signals—the order cannot be reversed. That's the core discipline of this chapter. If you look at KDJ first, you'll "see the signal you want to see" and then look back to find the trend to back it up—that's not judgment, that's making excuses. Once the order is reversed, discipline becomes something you "only follow when you're in a good mood."

qa.q: 前面的趨勢方法＋這裡的KDJ，為什麼是「天衣無縫」的搭檔？缺一個會怎樣？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 缺一個，你就只會「半套」。之前的趨勢組合方法有效解決趨勢問題，KDJ解決具體買賣問題，把二者有機結合才能既定向又落實買賣，配合無間。只懂趨勢，你知道「該往東」卻永遠不知道「何時邁步」；只懂KDJ，你天天邁步卻不知道「該不該往東」——兩個半套湊不成一套，只會湊成兩倍的錯誤。你怕承認自己只有半套。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 Miss one, and you'll only have "half the package." The previous trend combination method effectively solves the trend problem, while KDJ solves the specific buy/sell problem. Combine the two organically, and you'll have both direction and execution, working together seamlessly. If you only understand trends, you know "you should go east" but never know "when to take the step." If you only understand KDJ, you take steps every day but don't know "whether you should be going east." Two halves don't make a whole—they just make twice the mistakes. You're afraid to admit you only have half the package.

qa.q: 作者把「先看清楚趨勢」放在預測支撐壓力的第一步——不先看，會怎樣？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 會「一切空談」。首先要看清楚趨勢。因為趨勢決定一切，如果沒有趨勢的話，一切都是空談。沒有趨勢的支撐壓力，就像沒有地基的樓——你畫的每一條線都像真的，但全是浮沙上畫的；先看趨勢，等於先確認「這塊地能不能蓋樓」。你怕承認自己總是直接開畫。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 Then everything becomes "empty talk." First, you need to see the trend clearly. Because the trend decides everything—if there's no trend, everything is just empty talk. Support and resistance without a trend is like a building without a foundation—every line you draw looks real, but it's all drawn on quicksand. Looking at the trend first is like confirming "can this land even support a building?" You're afraid to admit you just start drawing right away.

qa.q: 「趨勢向上只有支撐、沒有壓力」——這句話，違反你的哪條直覺？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 違反「漲高了總該有壓力」的直覺。判斷趨勢上下是第一步，接下來要明白趨勢向上時股價只有支撐而沒有壓力，趨勢向下時只有壓力而沒有支撐，並須時刻銘記、付諸實踐。你總覺得「漲這麼多，該有壓力了吧」——那是用「價位」想事情，而規律是用「趨勢」想事情：順勢時每一道坎都是臺階，逆勢時每一塊平地都是懸崖。你怕承認自己盼它跌。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 It goes against the intuition that "after climbing so high, there must be some resistance." Judging whether the trend is up or down is the first step. Next, you need to understand that when the trend is up, the stock only has support and no resistance; when the trend is down, it only has resistance and no support—and you must always remember this and put it into practice. You always think, "It's already risen so much, shouldn't there be resistance?"—that's thinking in terms of "price," but the rule is thinking in terms of "trend." With the trend, every hurdle is a step; against the trend, every flat patch is a cliff. You're afraid to admit you're hoping it drops.

qa.q: 同樣的價位，為什麼「漲勢裡是支撐、跌勢裡是壓力」？線還是那條線，誰變了？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 變的是「勢」。當趨勢向上的時候，股價只有支撐而沒有壓力；反之趨勢向下時只有壓力而沒有支撐，這是判斷支撐壓力極重要的一點。同一條均線，多頭裡是地板、空頭裡是天花板——你以為支撐壓力是「畫在圖上的」，其實它是「長在趨勢上的」；不認趨勢，你連地板上天花板都分不清。你怕承認自己分不清地板天花板。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 What changes is the "trend." When the trend is up, the stock only has support and no resistance; conversely, when the trend is down, it only has resistance and no support. This is a super important point for judging support and resistance. The same moving average is a floor in an uptrend and a ceiling in a downtrend. You think support and resistance are "drawn on the chart," but really they "grow on the trend." If you don't recognize the trend, you can't even tell a floor from a ceiling. You're afraid to admit you can't tell the floor from the ceiling.

qa.q: MA憑什麼說自己能「準確反映支撐壓力在什麼價位」？它比其他工具強在哪？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 強在「給出數字」。MA預測壓力、支撐是其優勢，能夠準確地反映出股價壓力和支撐在什麼價位，讓投資人清楚知道支撐壓力所在的具體價位。別的判斷給你「大概、可能、感覺」，MA給你「就是這裡」——知道具體價位，你才知道該在哪掛單、該在哪停損；模糊的判斷，只能配上模糊的操作。你怕承認自己從不算價位。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 The strength lies in "giving you numbers." MA predicts pressure and support, and it does this well — it accurately shows exactly what price levels the pressure and support are at, so investors clearly know the specific prices where support and resistance sit. Other methods give you "maybe, probably, feels like," but MA tells you "right here." When you know the exact price, you know where to place your order and where to set your stop loss. Vague judgments can only lead to vague trading. You're afraid to admit you've never actually calculated the levels.

qa.q: 同樣是MA，為什麼有人用得好、有人一用就失真？問題出在哪個環節？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 出在「參數」。參數設置的不同直接影響其實戰效果，因此用好MA需要很高的專業知識，參數設置不當會使預測失真。參數是MA的命門——設對了，它是精準的尺；設錯了，它是會騙人的尺；而多數人從沒想過「我為什麼用這個參數」，於是失真時還以為是市場錯了。你怕承認是尺錯了。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 The weakness is in the "parameters." Different parameter settings directly affect how it performs in practice, so using MA well takes a high level of expertise. Set the parameters wrong and the predictions get distorted. Parameters are MA's Achilles' heel — set them right, and it's a precise ruler; set them wrong, and it's a lying ruler. But most people never ask, "Why am I even using these parameters?" So when it gives a wrong signal, they blame the market instead. You're afraid to admit the ruler was the one that was off.

qa.q: 「學會設置參數」是用好MA的關鍵——那不會設置的人，該怎麼辦？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 要嘛學，要嘛換。學會設置均線參數是用好MA的關鍵問題；針對學習而言，在提高操作水平及工具先進性上，MA大有鑽研的餘地。參數不是裝飾，是你對「跟蹤哪種節奏」的表態——不想學的人，作者後面給了出路（expma）；想學的人，這裡就是練功房。怕就怕：不學，又嫌MA不靈。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 Either learn it, or switch it up. Knowing how to set moving average parameters is the key to using MA well. If you're willing to learn, there's a lot of room to improve your trading skills and get more out of the tool. Parameters aren't just decoration — they're your way of saying, "This is the rhythm I'm tracking." For those who don't want to learn, the author gives you a way out later (EXPMA). For those who want to learn, this is the training ground. The real problem is: you don't learn, and then you complain MA doesn't work.

qa.q: expma和MA「功能差不多、用法大同小異」——那換成expma的意義是什麼？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 意義在「省事且不輸」。兩者功能差不多、使用方法大同小異，都是依靠均線的位置以及走勢的上下來判斷支撐、壓力。既然用法一樣，差別就只在「參數誰來設」——MA要你自己設，expma專家替你設好了；功能相同、門檻更低，這就是它存在的意義。你怕承認自己隨便用一個就算了。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 The point is "easy and still not losing." The two work similarly and are used in basically the same way — both rely on moving average positions and the direction of the trend to judge support and pressure. Since the usage is the same, the only difference is "who sets the parameters." With MA, you have to set them yourself; with EXPMA, the experts already did it for you. Same function, lower barrier to entry — that's why it exists. You're afraid to admit you just use whatever and call it a day.

qa.q: 「參數是專家設好的」——這句話，對你這種「不會設參數的人」意味著什麼？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 意味著「有人替你踩過坑」。expma並不需要投資人設置技術指標的參數，參數是專家設置好的默認數值，省去了參數調整的麻煩。你還在為「5日還是10日還是21日」糾結時，expma直接給你一份「專家版」——不是說你笨，是說你不必重複發明輪子；把省下的時間拿去執行紀律，比拿去調參數划算得多。你怕自己還在調參數。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 It means "someone already took the hits for you." EXPMA doesn't require investors to set technical indicator parameters — the parameters are default values preset by experts, saving you the hassle of tuning things. While you're still agonizing over "5-day, 10-day, or 21-day?" EXPMA just hands you an "expert version." That's not saying you're dumb — it's saying you don't need to reinvent the wheel. Spend the time you saved on executing your rules, which is way better use than fiddling with parameters. You're afraid you're still stuck tweaking those settings.

qa.q: 「實戰更實用」——「實戰」兩個字，把標準從「理論」拉到了哪裡？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 拉到「你上場時到底行不行」。因為expma參數是專家設置好的默認數值，投資人無需自行設置參數，使用門檻更低，實戰中更為簡便實用。理論上MA更「自由」，實戰中自由往往等於「選擇困難」——戰場上沒人等你調好參數；expma贏的不是精度，是「拿起來就能用」。實用，就是對普通人最大的先進。你怕自己選了用不起的。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 It comes down to "whether you can actually perform when it's your turn." Since EXPMA's parameters are expert-set defaults, investors don't need to configure them — the bar is lower, and in practice it's simpler and more practical. In theory, MA gives you more "freedom," but in practice freedom often equals "choice paralysis." On the battlefield, nobody's waiting for you to finish tuning your indicators. EXPMA doesn't win on precision; it wins on being "ready to use right out of the box." Being practical is the biggest advancement for the average person. You're afraid you picked something you can't even afford to use.

qa.q: 「把技術問題歸納成五個問題、用電腦自動分析」——這套「絕招」，先幫你省掉什麼？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 省掉「情緒」和「勞累」。主張「化繁為簡、安全賺錢」：把股票投資的技術問題歸納為趨勢、買賣點、主力成本價、選股、止損五個問題，用電腦程式組合63種指標自動分析，既降低工作強度又提高可靠性。多數人輸在「想太多、做太雜」——五個問題是「化繁」，電腦執行是「為簡」；人負責判斷，機器負責不帶感情地執行。你怕自己不敢交出去。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 It cuts out the "emotion" and the "grind." The philosophy is "simplify the complex, make money safely": boil stock investing down to five questions — trend, entry/exit points, main force cost price, stock selection, and stop loss — then use a computer program to combine 63 indicators for automatic analysis. That reduces the workload and boosts reliability. Most people lose because they "think too much and do too much." The five questions are the "simplifying," and the computer execution is the "streamlining." Humans handle judgment, machines handle emotionless execution. You're afraid you can't bring yourself to hand it over.

qa.q: 單一指標「理解容易」，為什麼偏偏「解決不了問題」？這兩件事矛盾在哪？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 不矛盾，就像認識字不等於會寫文章。單一指標不能解決複雜的股價運行趨勢、價格高低、能量是否充足等問題，必須將不同類型的技術指標組合在一起，相互取長補短，纔能有效解決股票投資的全部問題。單一指標只會答「一題」，市場考的是「綜合卷」——你只會做單選題，卻抱怨綜合卷太難，問題不在卷子，在你只練了一種題型。你怕承認偏科的是自己。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 Not contradictory at all — it's like knowing Chinese characters doesn't make you a writer. A single indicator can't solve complex problems like price trends, price levels, or whether volume is sufficient. You need to combine different types of indicators so they complement each other — that's the only way to effectively tackle the full picture of stock investing. A single indicator only answers "one question," but the market gives you a "comprehensive exam." You've only practiced multiple-choice, yet you complain the exam is too hard. The problem isn't the exam — it's that you only drilled one question type. You're afraid to admit the one who's unprepared is you.

qa.q: 「人是感情動物」——這五個字，說破了你分析時哪個不自覺的動作？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 說破「替自己找理由」的動作。人是感情動物，分析時會攙雜個人情感傾向，使結果偏離市場實際存在；電腦不帶感情偏差，既能提高工作效率，又能提高分析結果的可靠性。你「分析」時，其實常常在「論證自己已經想買的事」——先有結論，再找證據；電腦沒有「想買的股票」，所以它不會騙你，只有人會。你怕承認騙你的是自己。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 Let's call it what it is—making excuses for yourself. People are emotional creatures, so when we analyze, we mix in our own biases, pulling results away from what the market's actually doing. Computers don't have emotional baggage—they boost both efficiency and reliability. When you're "analyzing," you're really just "arguing for the stock you already wanna buy"—conclusion first, evidence later. A computer doesn't have a "stock it wants to buy," so it can't lie to you. Only people can. You're afraid to admit the one fooling you is you.

qa.q: 「趨勢是龍頭」——這四個字，怎麼解釋你「方向對了卻不賺錢」的怪現象？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 因為你只解決了「半個龍頭」。不明趨勢則不明方向，不明方向則不明買賣，不明買賣也就談不上賺錢；趨勢不僅解決方向問題，最主要的是能徹底解決持股還是持幣的時間週期長短的戰略問題。趨勢是龍頭，不只是「往哪走」，更是「走多久、該拿多久」——你方向對了，卻在該持股時天天想賣、該持幣時天天想買，龍頭就斷在你手裡。你怕承認自己拿不住。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 Because you've only solved "half the puzzle." Without understanding the trend, you don't know the direction; without direction, you don't know when to buy or sell; and without that, there's no making money. Trends solve not just direction, but more importantly the big strategic question—how long to hold stocks versus hold cash. Trend is the head honcho—it's not just "which way to go," it's "how long to ride, how long to hold." You got the direction right, but when you should hold, you wanna sell every day; when you should stay in cash, you wanna buy every day—you've cut the head off the trend right in your own hands. You're afraid to admit you can't hold.

qa.q: 趨勢看對了、股票選對了，為什麼還可能虧？作者說「最終落腳點」在哪？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 落在「買賣點」上。投資成敗最終要付諸實踐，買賣點就是付諸實踐的唯一手段，必須通過買賣才能達到賺錢的目的，因此準確把握買賣點是股票賺錢的最終落腳點。看對方向卻在錯誤的價位進出，就像看對了路卻在錯誤的站臺上車——理論全對，執行全錯；買賣點不是技巧問題，是「把對的判斷變成錢」的最後一公里。你怕自己錯在最後一步。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 It all comes down to "entry and exit points." Investment success or failure ultimately has to be put into practice—buy and sell points are the only way to do that. You've gotta actually buy and sell to make money, so nailing those points is the final destination for profitable trading. Getting the direction right but entering or exiting at the wrong price is like knowing the road but boarding at the wrong station—theory's all right, execution's all wrong. Buy/sell points aren't a skill issue; they're the last mile between "right call" and "real money." You're afraid you'll mess up the final step.

qa.q: 把價格指標「組合」成主力成本價——作者為什麼不直接看股價高低？「成本價」多告訴你什麼？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 多告訴你「主力賺不賺」。把傳統技術指標中有關價格分析的指標組合之後創造主力成本價指標，用來區分高價、低價問題，並把成本價分為三種：浮動成本價、盈利成本價、護住本金成本價。股價高低是「數字」，成本價是「立場」——知道主力手上是浮動、盈利還是護住本金，你就知道它急不急、會怎麼做；只看股價的人，等於只看計分板、不看球員狀態。你怕只看分數。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 Let me tell you more about "whether the big players are making money." By combining price-analysis indicators from traditional technical tools, we create a main-force cost price indicator to distinguish high vs. low prices. The cost price is split into three types: floating cost, profit cost, and principal-protection cost. Whether a stock price is high or low is just a "number"—cost price is a "position." Once you know whether the main force is sitting on floating, profit, or principal-protection, you know if they're in a hurry and what they'll do. People who only watch price are just staring at the scoreboard without checking the players' condition. You're afraid of only looking at the score.

qa.q: 「基本面確定，再參考技術面」——這個順序，為什麼不能反過來？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 因為技術面回答「何時」，基本面回答「何物」。單純技術面選股可交給電腦解決，但選股不能單純依靠技術面，更主要的是結合基本面；在基本面確定的前提下再參考技術面，這是選股的原則。先技術後基本面，等於先看「怎麼開車」再問「要去哪」——車技再好，開錯方向只是更快到達錯誤；順序反了，越努力越危險。你怕自己常開錯方向。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 Because technicals answer "when," and fundamentals answer "what." Picking stocks purely on technicals can be handed to a computer, but you can't rely on technicals alone—you've got to combine fundamentals. Use fundamentals as the baseline, then reference technicals—that's the principle. Technicals first, fundamentals second, is like asking "how do I drive?" before "where am I going?"—good driving skills just get you to the wrong place faster. Get the order backwards, and the harder you try, the more dangerous it gets. You're afraid you're always heading the wrong way.

qa.q: 「先活下來，再談賺錢」——「活下來」三個字，為什麼比「賺錢」更優先？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 因為死了就沒有「再」字。股市上首要考慮是讓自己盡可能長時間地活下來，其次纔是賺錢；要較長時間活下來唯一方法就是保證資金安全，而保證資金安全的唯一手段就是止損。賺錢是「之後」的事，活下來是「現在」的事——一次不止損的重創，可能抵掉你十年賺的錢；你以為止損是認輸，其實止損是「留著命繼續玩」。你怕承認不止損是怕認輸。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 Because if you're dead, there's no "next time." In the stock market, your first priority is to survive as long as possible; making money comes second. The only way to survive long-term is to protect your capital, and the only way to protect capital is to cut losses. Making money is "later"; staying alive is "right now." One devastating no-stop-loss loss can wipe out ten years of gains. You think stop-loss is admitting defeat, but really it's "keeping your seat at the table." You're afraid to admit that not stopping out is just fear of losing.

qa.q: 「8次賺3%、2次虧20%，還是虧」——這個算術題，為什麼多數人算不清？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 因為多數人只會「算贏的次數」。投資股票只是為了賺錢，不是為了成功率：10次交易8次各賺3%、2次各虧20%，結果還是虧損；反過來為保資金安全及時止損、有機會長期持有，8次各虧10%、2次各賺100%，整體卻盈利。賺的次數多不代表賺錢——「勝率」是面子，「盈虧比」是裡子；你天天數自己贏幾次，卻從不算自己虧多少，帳怎麼會平？
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 Because most people only count "how many times they win." You invest to make money, not to boost a win rate: 10 trades, 8 winning 3% each, 2 losing 20% each—still a net loss. Flip it: protect capital with timely stops, hold when opportunity’s there—8 losing 10% each, 2 winning 100% each—you end up profitable overall. Winning more often doesn't mean making money—"win rate" is the ego, "risk-reward ratio" is the real deal. You count your wins every day but never tally your losses—how's the books ever gonna balance?

qa.q: 一套「中國散戶的方法」被美國公司引進——這個事實，說服你的是什麼？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 說服你「規律不分國界」。到2003年通過計算軟件實現全部技術分析已達較高水平，該方法對外匯市場的分析在2005年被美國多家公司引入，其化繁為簡、安全賺錢的理念最受美國專業投資商讚賞。散戶以為高手都有獨門祕訣，其實被專業機構看中的是「化繁為簡」和「安全」——人家買的不是祕訣，是紀律；而你還在找祕訣。你怕承認紀律就是祕訣。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 Let me convince you that "rules don't know borders." By 2003, our software had already reached a high level in full technical analysis, and by 2005, multiple US firms adopted this method for forex markets. Its philosophy of simplifying complexity and earning safely is exactly what American professional investors appreciate most. Retail traders think pros all have secret formulas—but what institutions really value is "simplifying complexity" and "safety." They're not buying secrets; they're buying discipline. And you're still hunting for secrets. You're afraid to admit discipline IS the secret.

qa.q: 行情一動，你第一個念頭是「為什麼漲跌」還是「我該怎麼辦」？你多數時間在問哪一個？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 書中主張：股價漲跌是客觀存在，不是要探討研究的問題；投資人最主要考慮的是如何應對——漲時買入耐心持有，跌時賣出空倉持幣。多數人虧錢不是因為不懂漲跌原因，而是把力氣全花在解釋行情上，從沒替「應對」立過一條規則。解釋是事後諸葛，應對纔是當下能執行的動作。你怕承認自己從沒立過規則。
keywords: 你多數時間在問哪一個
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 The book's stance: price movements are objective reality, not something to be studied or debated. What investors really need to think about is how to respond—buy when it's rising and hold patiently, sell when it's falling and stay in cash. Most people lose money not because they don't understand why prices move, but because they pour all their energy into explaining the market, without ever setting a single rule for how to respond. Explaining is just hindsight; responding is the action you can actually take right now. You're afraid to admit you've never set any rules.

qa.q: 上漲中的每一次回調都讓你想下車、下跌中的每一次反彈都讓你想上車——你被「價位」牽著走過幾次？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 漲跌指的是趨勢而非具體價格變化。上漲中不斷有回調使投資人不敢介入，下跌中不斷有反彈使投資人不肯賣出；重價位而輕趨勢，正是上漲空倉、下跌滿倉的根源。你盯的是那一兩塊錢的震盪，而趨勢已經走完了整段路。你怕承認自己是被價位牽著走的。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 When we talk about ups and downs, we mean trends, not specific price movements. During an uptrend, pullbacks keep investors from jumping in; during a downtrend, bounces keep them from selling. Focusing on price levels while ignoring the trend—that's exactly why people end up empty-handed in rallies and fully loaded in crashes. You're staring at that one or two dollar wiggle, while the trend has already run the whole road. You're afraid to admit you've been led around by price levels.

qa.q: 你判斷趨勢靠的是「多學幾個指標」，還是「搞懂一個指標為什麼有效」？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 智能趨勢神經線的構造原理是：趨勢變化只是能量變化的外部表現，能量纔是內因；把反映趨勢與能量的技術指標按重要性分配不同權值，加權處理後以特殊形式表現出來指導買賣。關鍵不在指標多少，而在你懂不懂它衡量的是什麼——不懂原理就疊加指標，只是把混亂放大。你怕承認自己不懂它在衡量什麼。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 The way the Smart Trend Neural Line is built: trend changes are just the outer expression of energy changes—energy is the real driver. It takes the technical indicators that reflect trend and energy, assigns different weights based on importance, processes them with weighting, and presents them in a special form to guide buying and selling. The key isn't how many indicators you use, but whether you understand what they're measuring. Piling up indicators without understanding the logic just amplifies the chaos. You're afraid to admit you don't know what it's measuring.

qa.q: 同一套工具，有人用得順手、有人用起來就虧——你覺得差別出在哪裡？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 創造智能趨勢指標的關鍵難點不在選取多少技術指標，而在每個指標所佔的權重分配比例；權重分配解決得越好，指標對趨勢的把握越接近實際，否則偏差越大。工具背後的「權重」就是你的判斷力——你只會用工具，卻從不問它為什麼這樣配比，等於把最關鍵的決定交給了默認值。你怕承認權重是別人替你決定的。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 The real challenge in creating the Smart Trend Indicator isn't picking how many technical indicators to use—it's deciding the weight distribution for each one. The better the weight distribution, the closer the indicator tracks the actual trend; otherwise, the deviation grows. The 'weights' behind the tool are your judgment. You just use the tool, never asking why it's weighted that way—basically leaving the most critical decision to the default. You're afraid to admit those weights were decided by someone else.

qa.q: 趨勢線明天變成綠色，你手裡的股票會第一時間賣出，還是先「再看看」？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 紅色代表多頭上漲趨勢，堅持持倉、滿倉等候利潤最大化；綠色代表空頭下降趨勢，堅持空倉、清倉持幣耐心等待機會；黃色代表橫盤觀望趨勢，半倉操作、一半資金一半股票。規則簡單到可以背誦，難的是顏色變綠那一刻，你的手肯不肯聽規則的。你怕承認變綠那刻自己會討價還價。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 Red means a bullish uptrend—hold your position, stay fully invested and wait to maximize profits. Green means a bearish downtrend—stay in cash, clear your position and patiently wait for opportunities. Yellow means a sideways, wait-and-see trend—go half in, half cash, half stocks. The rules are simple enough to memorize; the hard part is the moment the color turns green—whether your hand is willing to follow the rules. You're afraid to admit that in that moment, you'd try to negotiate.

qa.q: 「怕買了跌、怕賣了漲」——你被這兩個「怕」左右過多少次？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 因為價格上漲時不斷有回調，投資人不敢介入生怕進去後下跌；下跌時不斷有反彈，投資人不決心賣出擔心賣後上漲；不重視趨勢而重視價位變動，又缺乏可靠有效的工具解決趨勢問題。你的每一次進出都建立在「怕」之上——而怕，正是趨勢最大的敵人。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 Because when prices rise, there are always pullbacks, and investors hesitate to jump in for fear it might drop after they enter. When prices fall, there are always bounces, and investors can't make up their minds to sell, worried it might go back up. They don't respect the trend, only the price movement—and without reliable, effective tools to solve the trend problem. Every entry and exit you make is built on fear—and fear is the biggest enemy of the trend.

qa.q: 趨勢線顏色沒變，你卻頻繁進出——你在操作市場，還是在操作自己的焦慮？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 顏色不變則表明趨勢沒有發生變化，顏色變了就說明趨勢已發生變化；其最大實戰意義在於指導投資者根據趨勢變化，保證倉位變化與市場變化相一致。顏色沒變而你在動，動的不是倉位，是情緒——市場沒變，是你受不了「什麼都不做」。你怕承認，坐不住的是你。
keywords: 還是在操作自己的焦慮
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 If the color doesn't change, it means the trend hasn't changed; if the color changes, it means the trend has shifted. The biggest practical value is guiding investors to align their position changes with market changes based on trend shifts. If the color hasn't changed and you're moving, what's moving isn't your position—it's your emotions. The market hasn't changed; you just can't stand 'doing nothing.' You're afraid to admit that the one who can't sit still is you.

qa.q: 你買一個工具，是為了用它解決一個問題，還是為了尋找「神奇功能」？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 智能趨勢神經線最主要的功能就是把握趨勢，簡單地應用它把握趨勢即可，不要去捉摸還有沒有其他神奇用途，以免偏離指標的本質作用。人總想在工具裡找魔法——找到最後，魔法沒有，偏離本質的虧損倒有一堆。你怕承認自己在找魔法。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 The main function of the Smart Trend Neural Line is to grasp the trend. Just apply it simply for that purpose—don't go hunting for other magical uses, or you'll drift away from the indicator's core purpose. People always look for magic in tools—and in the end, there's no magic, just a pile of losses from straying off course. You're afraid to admit you've been looking for magic.

qa.q: 你進場那一刻，先想的是「能賺多少」，還是「虧多少我必須走」？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 本章主張止損信號主要為保證資金安全。股市風險很大，進入市場那一刻就承擔了全部風險，因此資金安全在風險市場是首要考慮的問題。只算賺多少的人，虧損時沒有退路；先想好「虧多少就走」的人，纔有資格談賺錢——因為他先保證了自己還活著。你怕承認自己從沒想過虧多少就走。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 This chapter's main point is that stop-loss signals are primarily about protecting your capital. The stock market is risky—the moment you enter, you're taking on full risk, so capital safety is the #1 concern in a risky market. People who only count how much they can make have no escape route when losses hit; those who first think about "how much loss means I'm out" are the ones who deserve to talk about making money—because they've made sure they're still alive first. You're afraid to admit you've never actually thought about how much loss would make you walk away.

qa.q: 你總想「等它再漲一點就賣、再跌一點就買」——你在等的那個「點」，到底是什麼？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 止損信號依據趨勢反轉時形成的轉點：多頭向空頭、空頭向多頭轉換時必然有轉點出現，及時把握該轉點當作止損信號，是最巧妙也最科學的方法。你不是在等「點」，是在等一個讓自己舒服的價位——而趨勢轉折時，從來沒有舒服的價位。你怕承認自己在等舒服的價位。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 The stop-loss signal is based on the turning point formed when the trend reverses: when bulls turn to bears, or bears to bulls, a turning point is bound to appear. Catching that point in time as your stop-loss signal is the most elegant and most scientific method. You're not waiting for a "point"—you're waiting for a price you're comfortable with. But when the trend turns, there is never a comfortable price. You're afraid to admit you're waiting for a comfortable price.

qa.q: 同樣一句「賣出」，為什麼別人執行得了、你卻總覺得「不適合我」？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 止損分空頭止損與多頭止損，對期貨、外匯雙邊市容易理解，對單邊的國內股市喫力；為讓人人理解引用，作者將止損信號與買賣點結合統一表示，符合簡單操作理念。規則的設計是為了讓人人能執行——你說「不適合」，往往不是規則複雜，而是你不肯承認規則考驗的是執行力。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 There are two kinds of stop-loss—short-side and long-side. It's easy to understand in two-way markets like futures or forex, but harder in a one-way domestic stock market. To make it clear for everyone, the author combines stop-loss signals with buy/sell points into one unified expression, keeping it simple and practical. Rules are designed so anyone can follow them—when you say "it doesn't suit me," it's often not that the rule is complicated, but that you won't admit the rule is testing your discipline.

qa.q: 提示說「逢高賣出」，你手裡還有股票——你會全部清倉，還是留一點「再看看」？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 當手頭持有股票、看到逢高賣出提示的時候，就全部賣掉股票清倉，不猶豫、不保留。留的那一點「再看看」，往往就是你把利潤還回去的那一點——猶豫的本質，是你寧願相信自己的判斷，也不相信規則。你怕承認自己寧願信判斷不信規則。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 When you're holding stocks and you see the "sell on strength" signal, just sell everything and go to full cash—no hesitation, no holding back. That little bit you keep "just to watch" is usually the little bit where you give your profits back. Hesitation is basically you trusting your own judgment over the rules. You're afraid to admit you'd rather trust your gut than the rules.

qa.q: 提示說「逢低買入」，你敢滿倉嗎？還是總想等一個「更低的價」？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 當手頭持有資金空倉、看到逢低買入提示的時候，就全部買入股票滿倉持有。不敢滿倉，是因為你怕買完就跌；可規則要的不是「買在最低」，是「信號出現就執行」——你等的那個「更低」，常常是趨勢已經走完的證據。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 When you're holding cash and you see the "buy on dips" signal, just go all in with full position. The reason you don't dare go full is you're scared it'll drop right after you buy. But the rule isn't asking for the "lowest price"—it's asking you to execute when the signal appears. That "lower price" you're waiting for is often just proof that the trend has already played out.

qa.q: 提示說「半倉」，你卻總想「這次我全倉」——你憑什麼覺得自己比規則聰明？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 滿倉就減掉一半股票，空倉就拿一半資金買入股票，無論當前是滿倉還是空倉都按提示減半或買入半倉。半倉是規則對不確定性的承認；你全倉，是覺得自己看穿了不確定性——而市場最擅長懲罰這種自信。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 If you're fully invested, cut half your position; if you're in cash, use half your capital to buy in. Whether you're full or empty, just follow the signal and go half in or half out. A half position is the rule acknowledging uncertainty. Going full means you think you've seen through it—and the market loves to punish that kind of confidence.

qa.q: 信號一天變好幾次，你的第一反應是「這工具不準」，還是「市場正在選擇方向」？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 此時市場在選擇方向，止損買賣信號非常頻繁。切不可把保護資金安全的靈敏優勢誤以為不準確，這恰恰是它的優勢所在。你把靈敏當失靈，是因為你受不了「不確定」——可橫盤的本質就是不確定，信號頻繁只是在忠實地告訴你：現在別亂動。你怕承認自己受不了不確定。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 At this point the market is choosing a direction, so stop-loss buy/sell signals are very frequent. Don't mistake this sensitive edge for inaccuracy—it's precisely the strength here. You see sensitivity as unreliability because you can't stand "uncertainty." But the essence of a sideways market is uncertainty, and the frequent signals are just honestly telling you: don't move around right now. You're afraid to admit you can't stand the uncertainty.

qa.q: 一個「反應遲鈍」的中長線指標，和一個「很靈敏」的止損信號同時出現，你信哪個？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 中長線指標對價格變動反應遲鈍，止損買賣信號卻根據趨勢而來、優於趨勢，在有效穩定判斷趨勢的狀態下還能保持如此靈敏。靈敏不是錯，是它比遲鈍的指標更早看見轉折——你嫌它太敏感，其實是嫌真相來得太快。你怕承認自己嫌真相太快。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 Mid-to-long-term indicators are slow to react to price changes, but stop-loss buy/sell signals are driven by the trend and actually lead it—they stay effective at confirming the trend while remaining this sensitive. Sensitivity isn't a flaw; it sees the turning point earlier than dull indicators do. You complain it's too sensitive, but really, you're complaining the truth comes too fast. You're afraid to admit you hate how fast the truth arrives.

qa.q: 你知道頻繁交易是虧損之源，但你為什麼還是停不下來？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 頻繁交易是導致虧損的因素之一，作者因此創造了一個約束交易次數的技術指標哈瑞隨機指標，用以避免信號靈敏引發的過度交易。停不下來，不是因為機會太多，而是因為你把「動手」誤當成「勤奮」——市場獎勵的是少而準的出手，不是多而亂的動作。你怕承認自己把動手誤當勤奮。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 Frequent trading is one of the factors that leads to losses. That's why the author created the Hurry Random Indicator—a technical tool designed to limit how often you trade, so you don't over-trade from overly sensitive signals. You can't stop not because there are too many opportunities, but because you've mistaken "acting" for "being diligent." The market rewards fewer, precise moves—not a bunch of messy ones. You're afraid to admit that you've been confusing action with diligence.

qa.q: 你買股票時，想過「是誰在推動這支股票的價格」嗎？還是隻看新聞和消息面？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 書中主張：股價變動受一雙無形的手調節——即大資金。只有大資金的買賣才能引起股價甚至趨勢改變，小資金的影響幾乎可忽略。你以為自己在跟市場博弈，其實你在跟一雙你看不見的手博弈；不承認它的存在，你連對手是誰都不知道。
keywords: 還是隻看新聞和消息面
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 The book argues that price movements are regulated by an invisible hand—big money. Only big money's buying and selling can move prices or even shift trends; small money's impact is almost negligible. You think you're playing against the market, but really you're playing against a hand you can't see. If you refuse to acknowledge it exists, you don't even know who your opponent is.

qa.q: 你總想「挖出莊家是誰」——但作者說不必知道是誰。你為什麼放不下這個執念？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 「引導市場趨勢的是主流資金」理念的核心是：不必知道資金是誰在操縱，但必須承認有這樣一個資金存在。西方有做市商專司引導趨勢，國內雖無合法機構，卻有機構資金受利益驅使暗中充當此角色。你執著於「找出誰」，其實是想為自己的虧損找一個具體的敵人——可敵人從來不是某個人，是你看不見的資金流向。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 The core idea behind "mainstream capital leads market trends" is this: you don't need to know who's behind the money, but you must admit that such money exists. In the West, there are market makers whose job is to guide trends. In China, there's no legal institution for that, but institutional capital still quietly plays that role, driven by self-interest. Your obsession with "finding out who" is really just you trying to find a concrete enemy for your losses—but the enemy was never a person. It's the flow of capital you can't see.

qa.q: 同一天裡，你既怕踏空又怕被套——你到底站在哪一邊？你分得清嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 因為同一個人在同一天內既可以是多方也可以是空方，用具體的人區分不科學；找不到對手就必輸無疑，故須以多空劃分，並設法找出判定多空的方法。你連自己是多是空都說不清，卻指望贏過那些立場分明的人——立場模糊，是散戶最常見的輸法。你怕承認，自己也是這樣輸的。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 Because the same person can be both a bull and a bear on the same day, it's not scientific to classify by specific people. If you can't find your opponent, you're guaranteed to lose. So you have to divide by long and short, and find a way to determine which side you're on. You can't even clearly say whether you're long or short, yet you expect to beat people who know exactly where they stand. Vague positioning is the most common way retail traders lose. You're afraid to admit that you've been losing that way too.

qa.q: 你判斷「誰是贏家」靠什麼？靠感覺，還是靠數據？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 颶風指標以成交量與股價變動幅度統計做多、做空兩股力量的角逐力度，把傳統趨勢判斷與能量判斷的技術指標作為計算因子，判斷力量向哪一方傾斜，讓投資人跟隨贏家。感覺會騙你——一根大陽線就能讓你把空方看成多方；數據統計的，纔是力量的持續傾斜。你怕承認，自己總信當天的心情。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 The Hurricane Indicator uses trading volume and price movement to measure the battle between bullish and bearish forces. It combines traditional trend judgment and momentum indicators as calculation factors to see which side is gaining strength, so investors can follow the winners. Feelings lie to you—one big green candle can make you see bears as bulls. But data shows where the real, sustained strength lies. You're afraid to admit that you always trust your mood of the day.

qa.q: 紅線、藍線、0位線——你能一眼說出現在誰站在0位線之上嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 紅色曲線代表做多的主力資金，藍色曲線代表做空的的主力資金，另有決定多空輸贏的0位線；0位線之上代表贏家，0位線之下代表輸家。這不是複雜的公式，是讓你把「跟贏家站在一起」變成看得見的動作——你做不到，是因為你總想跟「你喜歡的那一方」站在一起。你怕承認，自己輸在偏心。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 The red curve represents the main bullish capital, the blue curve represents the main bearish capital, and there's also a zero line that decides who wins. Above the zero line means winners; below means losers. This isn't a complicated formula—it's a visual way to make "stand with the winners" a concrete action. You can't do it because you always want to stand with the side you *like*. You're afraid to admit that you lose because of bias.

qa.q: 紅線向上交叉藍線並站上0位線，信號擺在你面前——你會照買，還是先懷疑「是不是騙線」？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 紅線由下向上交叉藍線並站在0位線之上，投資人應買入股票等候上漲；藍線由下向上交叉紅線並站在0位線之上，此時應賣出股票，等候股價進一步下跌。信號本身不複雜，複雜的是你總想替信號「把關」——而你的把關，往往是拿自己的判斷對抗機制的判斷。你怕承認，自己信不過規則。
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 When the red line crosses above the blue line from below and stays above the zero line, investors should buy and wait for the rise. When the blue line crosses above the red line from below and stays above the zero line, that's the time to sell and wait for further decline. The signal itself isn't complicated—what's complicated is that you always feel the need to "double-check" the signal. And your double-checking is usually just your own judgment fighting the system's judgment. You're afraid to admit that you don't trust the rules.

qa.q: 兩線將要交叉又忽然分開——這種「最像騙線」的形態，你敢信它是最佳買點嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 紅線在0位線上方運行一段時間後由上向下靠近0位線，藍線也從下向上靠近，兩線將要交叉時忽然再次分開，藍線掉頭向下、紅線掉頭向上，此時是最佳買入機會，多發生在長期下跌後上漲初期。最佳買點往往長得最像陷阱——因為市場就是用「像陷阱」來甩掉像你一樣猶豫的人。你怕承認，自己就是那個猶豫的人。
keywords: 你敢信它是最佳買點嗎
qa.a_en: Hey there! 😊 After the red line has been above the zero line for a while, it starts moving down toward the zero line, while the blue line also moves up from below. Just as the two lines are about to cross, they suddenly separate again—the blue turns back down, the red turns back up. That's the best buying opportunity, and it usually happens early in an uptrend after a long decline. The best entry point often looks exactly like a trap—because the market uses "looks like a trap" to shake off people who hesitate, just like you. You're afraid to admit that you're the one hesitating.

qa.q: 對應的賣出形態出現時，你捨得走嗎？還是總想「再漲一點」？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 藍線在0位線之上運行後由上向下靠近0位線，紅線也從下向上靠近，兩線將要交叉時忽然再次分開，藍線掉頭向上、紅線掉頭向下，此時是最佳賣出機會，多發生在長期上漲後下跌初期。「再漲一點」是貪婪的倒數計時——最佳賣點出現時不賣，你等來的往往是「再跌一點」。
keywords: 對應的賣出形態出現時
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 When the blue line runs above the zero line and then approaches it from top to bottom, while the red line also climbs up from below—just as the two lines are about to cross, they suddenly separate again, with the blue line turning back up and the red line turning back down—that's your best selling opportunity. This mostly happens in the early stage of a decline after a long uptrend. "Just a little higher" is the countdown to greed—when the best sell point shows up and you don't sell, what you're usually waiting for is "a little lower."

qa.q: 指標說信號會滯後、買點可能已漲了15%——你願意接受「不完美」的工具嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 颶風指標是中長線綜合類技術指標，發出信號往往滯後，買點距最低價已有約15%以上漲幅；激烈上漲中發出的買入信號因短期漲幅過大可能被套，作者故創造哈瑞隨機指標來化解。沒有完美的工具，只有接受工具侷限並用別的指標互補的人——你追求完美工具，追求到的往往是「什麼都不敢買」。你怕承認，完美是藉口。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 The Hurricane Indicator is a medium-to-long-term composite technical indicator, so its signals tend to lag—by the time it fires, the buy point is already about 15% or more above the lowest price. In a sharp rally, the buy signal it gives can leave you trapped because the short-term gain is already too big. That's why the author created the Harry Stochastic Indicator to fix that. There's no perfect tool—only people who accept a tool's limitations and use other indicators to complement it. Chase the perfect tool, and what you'll end up chasing is "too afraid to buy anything." You're afraid to admit that perfection is just an excuse.

qa.q: 你手上那支「總是不漲」的股票，你留著它，是因為它會漲，還是因為你捨不得認錯？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 本章主張：強者恆強、弱者恆弱，實戰中要盡可能選擇強勢股、堅決迴避弱勢股。你留著弱勢股，往往不是因為它會漲，而是因為「都跌這麼多了，總該反彈了吧」——這正是弱者恆弱最喜歡的投資人。你怕承認自己留著，是不甘心。
keywords: 還是因為你捨不得認錯
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 This chapter says: the strong stay strong, the weak stay weak—so in practice you should pick strong stocks whenever possible and firmly avoid weak ones. You hold onto weak stocks, usually not because they'll go up, but because "they've already dropped so much, they gotta bounce sometime, right?"—and that's exactly the kind of investor that "weak stays weak" loves. You're afraid to admit that holding on is really just unwillingness to let go.

qa.q: 你會不會在心裡對股市喊「它應該漲啊」？——你是在跟市場講道理，還是在跟自己講道理？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 股市有其內在規律，把自己的觀點強加到股市身上而希望股市尊重自己，無異於以卵擊石；2006年有多少人因不能適應市場遊戲規則，錯失一次千載難逢的股市大機遇。市場從不聽你講道理，它只按規則運行——你每一次「應該漲」的憤怒，都是在用情緒對抗規律。你怕承認，市場沒在聽你講道理。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 The stock market has its own internal rules. Forcing your opinions onto it and hoping it'll respect you is like throwing an egg at a rock. In 2006, how many people missed a once-in-a-lifetime market opportunity because they couldn't adapt to the game? The market never listens to your reasoning—it just follows its rules. Every time you get angry thinking "it should go up," you're using emotion to fight the rules. You're afraid to admit that the market isn't listening to your arguments.

qa.q: 你判斷一支股票強弱，憑的是成交量，還是憑「感覺它會漲」？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 股票由強到弱、由弱到強是漸變過程，這一切取決於成交量的變化，故判斷強弱的工具應從成交量入手；黃金線是組合指標，綜合市場存量資金與每日交易量、流通盤與成交量、換手及價格波動幅度等關係。感覺是滯後的——等你「感覺」到強，強勢往往已走完一半。你怕承認，自己的感覺總慢半拍。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 A stock's transition from strong to weak, or weak to strong, is a gradual process, and it all comes down to changes in trading volume. So the tools for judging strength should start with volume. The Golden Line is a composite indicator that combines relationships like market idle funds vs. daily trading volume, float vs. turnover, and turnover rate vs. price fluctuation range. Feelings lag—by the time you "feel" it's strong, the strong move is often already half over. You're afraid to admit that your feelings always run half a beat late.

qa.q: 股票價格能觸及生命禁區的纔是強者——你的股票，到得了那裡嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 生命禁區代表強勢區域，受自然界啟發：凡是能在青藏高原無人區生存的人一定是強者，弱者到不了生命禁區；股票價格能夠觸及生命禁區的，一定是強勢股票。你總想抄底弱者，但弱者之所以弱，就是因為它連生命禁區的門檻都摸不到。你怕承認，自己老在抄弱者。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 The Life Forbidden Zone represents the strong zone, inspired by nature: anyone who can survive in the no-man's-land of the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau has to be strong—the weak can't even reach it. Likewise, a stock price that can touch the Life Forbidden Zone is definitely a strong stock. You keep wanting to catch the falling knife on weak stocks, but the reason they're weak is that they can't even touch the threshold of the Life Forbidden Zone. You're afraid to admit that you're always bottom-fishing the weak.

qa.q: 股價掉進泥潭，每次反彈你都以為是機會——你知道反彈其實是什麼嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 股價泥潭代表弱勢區域，如同人掉進沼澤，晃動越厲害下降越快；股價一旦掉入泥潭，每次反彈都意味著新一輪下跌，你要做的就是扔掉它，免得越陷越深、血本無歸。你把反彈當機會，是因為你太想回到成本——而泥潭裡的反彈，是留給「捨不得走」的人的。你怕承認，留下是怕認輸。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 The Stock Price Quagmire represents the weak zone—like a person falling into a swamp: the more you struggle, the faster you sink. Once a stock price drops into the quagmire, every bounce just means another round of decline. All you need to do is throw it away before you sink deeper and lose everything. You see bounces as opportunities because you're too desperate to get back to your cost—but a bounce in the quagmire is for people who "can't bear to leave." You're afraid to admit that staying is really about being afraid to lose.

qa.q: 股價跌破生死線，說明行情結束了——你是把它當「離場信號」，還是當「抄底機會」？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 生死線是多空分水嶺，股票價格能夠上穿生死線才表示開始有了生機，可以開始關注；一旦向下跌破生死線，說明行情結束了，需要考慮離場的問題。你總在跌破生死線時想「跌這麼多總該反彈」——可生死線的含義恰恰相反：跌破，是結束，不是開始。你怕承認，自己總在結束時當開始。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 The Life-Death Line is the bull-bear dividing line. Only when a stock price breaks above the Life-Death Line does it show signs of life, and that's when you can start paying attention. Once it breaks below, it means the trend is over, and you need to think about exiting. You always think "it's dropped so much, it has to bounce" when it breaks below—but the Life-Death Line means exactly the opposite: breaking below is an ending, not a beginning. You're afraid to admit that you keep treating an ending as a beginning.

qa.q: 黃金線上穿生死線、直接進生命禁區——你手裡正好有它，你拿得住嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 當黃金線上穿生死線之後，直接進入生命禁區，或者經過不超過3個交易日的短暫回調進入生命禁區，表示該股票屬於強勢股票，應繼續持有。標準很清楚，難的是持有途中每一根陰線都在考驗你——拿不住強勢股，等於把標準背得滾瓜爛熟，卻從不執行。你怕承認，自己就是拿不住的人。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 When the golden line crosses above the life-and-death line and then goes straight into the danger zone—or enters it after a brief pullback of no more than 3 trading days—that means the stock is strong and you should keep holding. The standard is crystal clear. The hard part is that every single red candle along the way tests you—if you can't hold onto a strong stock, it's like memorizing the rules perfectly but never actually following them. You're afraid to admit that you're the one who can't hold.

qa.q: 黃金線下穿生死線、掉進泥潭——你給自己定過「賣掉清倉」的紀律嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 當黃金線從上向下下穿生死線，直接進入股價泥潭，或者在生死線之下經過不超過3個交易日的微弱反彈後進入股價泥潭，表示該股屬於弱勢股票，應考慮賣掉清倉。規則寫得明明白白，執行卻需要你承認「我買錯了」——承認錯誤，是弱勢股持有人最難的一課。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 When the golden line crosses below the life-and-death line from above and goes straight into the stock price quagmire—or enters it after a weak bounce of no more than 3 trading days below the line—that means the stock is weak and you should consider selling out completely. The rules are written in black and white, but executing them requires you to admit, "I bought the wrong one." Admitting that mistake is the hardest lesson for anyone holding a weak stock.

qa.q: 日線說弱、周線說強——兩個週期打架時，你聽誰的？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 當日線黃金線已下穿生死線而周線還在生命禁區的強勢區域，說明該股經過回調之後還有繼續走強的可能；相反，周線在股價泥潭而日線已上穿生死線，表明反彈之後還有可能繼續走弱。週期打架時，大週期是老闆——你只看日線，等於讓員工替老闆做決定。你怕承認，自己常讓員工拍板。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 When the daily golden line has already crossed below the life-and-death line but the weekly line is still in the strong zone of the danger zone, that means the stock could still strengthen again after the pullback. On the flip side, if the weekly line is in the quagmire but the daily line has already crossed above the life-and-death line, it suggests the stock may keep weakening after the bounce. When timeframes clash, the larger timeframe is the boss—if you only look at the daily chart, it's like letting an employee make decisions for the boss. You're afraid to admit that you often let the employee call the shots.

qa.q: 股價一頂比一頂高、指標卻一頂比一頂低——你看到的是「新高」，還是「警告」？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 股價一頂比一頂高而黃金線反而一頂比一頂低，表明股價有逐漸走弱的跡象需警惕；股價一底比一底低而黃金線一底比一底高，表明又開始走強需強烈關注；這種現象發生得越早，股票越有可能成為領頭羊。背離是市場在說真話——你聽不聽，決定了你是領頭羊還是接盤者。你怕承認，自己選擇看不見。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 When each price high is higher than the last but each golden line high is lower than the last, that's a warning sign the stock is gradually weakening—stay alert. When each price low is lower than the last but each golden line low is higher than the last, that means it's strengthening again and deserves serious attention. The earlier this divergence appears, the more likely the stock becomes a leader. Divergence is the market telling the truth—whether you listen decides if you're the leader or the bag holder. You're afraid to admit that you choose not to see it.

qa.q: 你買股票最怕的兩件事——「買了就套」和「錯過行情」——你總在兩者之間搖擺嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 本書主張用帶有強烈使命感的技術指標解決實戰難題：既不耽誤行情、短期內也不會被套，同時解決「有錢時最佳買點已錯過」的中途建倉問題。你搖擺，是因為你把「怕套」和「怕錯過」都當成大事——而紀律的作用，就是讓你在兩者之間不再靠情緒選擇。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 This book advocates using technical indicators with a strong sense of mission to solve real-world trading problems: neither missing the move nor getting trapped in the short term, while also solving the mid-entry problem when "the best buying point is already gone by the time you have money." You waver because you treat both "fear of being trapped" and "fear of missing out" as big deals—and the role of discipline is to keep you from deciding based on emotions between the two.

qa.q: 中長線信號出現時，短線漲幅已經很大——你追，還是不追？你憑什麼決定？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 哈瑞隨機指標帶著控制短期買賣風險、中途建倉的使命誕生。因為中長線買賣點較穩定，但信號出現時短線漲幅過大，執行易被套、不執行易錯過行情。追與不追，靠的不是勇氣，是另一個指標告訴你「現在是不是短線高點」——你憑感覺決定，等於把兩難交給運氣。你怕承認，自己一直在憑感覺。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 The Harry stochastic indicator was born with the mission of controlling short-term buying and selling risk and enabling mid-entry positioning. Since mid-to-long-term buy and sell points are more stable, but by the time signals appear the short-term rally is already too big—executing gets you trapped, not executing misses the move. Whether to chase or not doesn't depend on courage; it depends on another indicator telling you, "Is this a short-term high right now?"—if you decide by gut feeling, you're leaving that dilemma to luck. You're afraid to admit you've been going with your gut all along.

qa.q: 中長線說「趨勢走好可以買」，短線說「價格太高別追」——兩個聲音，你聽哪個？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 中長線依靠趨勢賺錢，短線依賴價格賺錢。趨勢已走好可買入時，短線指標可能認為價格太高失去參與價值，反而可以賣出。兩個聲音不是吵架，是分工：一個管方向，一個管價位——你把它們當成對立，是因為你總想要一個「非買即賣」的簡單答案。你怕承認，自己要的只是簡單。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 Mid-to-long-term strategies profit from trends; short-term strategies rely on price. When the trend has already turned bullish enough to buy, short-term indicators might say the price is too high to add value and could even be a sell signal. These two voices aren't fighting—they're dividing labor: one handles direction, the other handles price. You see them as opposites because you always want a simple "buy or sell" answer. You're afraid to admit that what you really want is just simplicity.

qa.q: K值、D值、J值、0~100等值線——你只知道「金叉買、死叉賣」，你知道它們各自在說什麼嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 哈瑞隨機指標由3條曲線構成，因構造上部分原理同KDJ，為方便起見分別稱K值、D值、J值；另一重要組成部分是0~100的等值線，實際使用功能有兩種。只記口訣不問原理，等於只看儀表不學駕駛——金叉死叉是結果，曲線的位置與關係纔是原因。你怕承認，自己只記了口訣。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 The Harry stochastic indicator is made up of three curves. Since some of its construction principles are similar to KDJ, for convenience they're called K, D, and J. Another important component is the 0–100 equal-value scale, which has two practical functions. If you just memorize the catchphrases without asking why, it's like only reading the dashboard without learning to drive—crossovers are the result, but the position and relationship of the curves are the cause. You're afraid to admit that you only memorized the catchphrases.

qa.q: 一輪上漲中每次回調都是機會——回調來臨時，你敢按信號買嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 發出短線買賣信號是其主要功能，必須與颶風智能趨勢神經線配合使用；在一輪上漲行情中很善於捕捉每次回調之後的機會並及時發出買入信號。你不敢在回調時買，是因為你把「下跌」和「危險」畫了等號——而在紅色趨勢裡，回調是上車點，不是逃生門。你怕承認，自己把下跌當危險。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 Its main function is to generate short-term buy and sell signals, and it must be used together with the Hurricane Intelligent Trend Neural Line. In a rising market, it’s great at catching opportunities after every pullback and sending out buy signals in time. You don’t dare to buy on a pullback because you’ve drawn an equal sign between “falling” and “danger” — but in a red trend, a pullback is a boarding point, not an escape door. You’re afraid to admit that you’ve been treating a drop as danger.

qa.q: 趨勢線紅色、金叉出現——信號說「買」，你的手在猶豫什麼？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 出現哈瑞隨機指標金叉應買入，這是捕捉回調後機會的短線買入信號，在紅色趨勢下配合使用短線效果奇佳。猶豫，是因為你總想「再確認一下」——可規則已經確認過了；你反覆確認的不是信號，是你對自己判斷的不信任。你怕承認，確認是拖延的藉口。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 When the Hurry Stochastic Indicator gives a golden cross, you should buy. This is a short-term buy signal that catches opportunities after a pullback, and it works amazingly for short-term trading when combined with a red trend. Your hesitation comes from always wanting to “confirm one more time” — but the rules have already confirmed it. What you keep confirming isn’t the signal; it’s your distrust in your own judgment. You’re afraid to admit that confirming is just an excuse to procrastinate.

qa.q: 死叉預示要回調——你手裡有股票，你忍得住不賣嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 出現死叉預示要回調：手頭持有股票不需賣出；準備買入者應暫時迴避，等候發出買入提示時再買入。規則說「不用賣」，你卻總想「先跑為敬」——因為你分不清「預示回調」和「趨勢結束」，而規則替你分清了，你不信它。你怕承認，跑是怕被套。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 When a death cross shows up, it signals a pullback: if you’re holding stocks, you don’t need to sell; if you’re planning to buy, you should stay away for now and wait for a buy signal before entering. The rules say “no need to sell,” but you always want to “run first” — because you can’t tell the difference between “signaling a pullback” and “trend over.” The rules have already told them apart for you, but you don’t trust them. You’re afraid to admit that running is because you’re afraid of getting trapped.

qa.q: 中長線喊「買」，短線喊「太高了」——你敢違背其中一個聲音嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 中長線指標發出買入提示，但哈瑞隨機指標在60以上死叉或高於80，應暫時不要買入，耐心等候回調；回調之後趨勢線依然紅色、金叉發出短線買入信號時再買入，因行情接近尾聲或剛啟動漲幅過大、分歧較大。敢「不買」，比敢「買」更難——因為它要求你對抗「錯過行情」的恐懼，而恐懼最會偽裝成機會。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 When the mid-to-long-term indicator gives a buy signal, but the Hurry Stochastic Indicator shows a death cross above 60 or is above 80, you should hold off and patiently wait for a pullback. After the pullback, if the trend line is still red and a golden cross triggers a short-term buy signal, then buy — because the market might be near the end, or just started with too big a move, and there’s a lot of disagreement. Daring “not to buy” is harder than daring “to buy” — because it asks you to fight the fear of “missing the market,” and fear is best at disguising itself as opportunity.

qa.q: 中長線喊「賣」，短線喊「別急」——你能按規則「再等等」嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 中長線指標發出賣出提示，但哈瑞隨機指標在40以下金叉時，暫時不要賣出，耐心等候反彈；反彈之後趨勢線依然綠色、死叉發出短線賣出信號時再賣出。「再等等」不是拖延，是規則讓你在更好的價位離場——你分不清「等反彈」和「等回到成本」，是因為後者纔是你真正想要的。你怕承認，自己等的是藉口。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 When the mid-to-long-term indicator gives a sell signal, but the Hurry Stochastic Indicator shows a golden cross below 40, don’t sell for now; wait patiently for a rebound. After the rebound, if the trend line is still green and a death cross gives a short-term sell signal, then sell. “Wait a little longer” isn’t procrastination — the rules are letting you exit at a better price. You can’t tell the difference between “waiting for a rebound” and “waiting to break even,” because the latter is what you really want. You’re afraid to admit that what you’re waiting for is an excuse.

qa.q: 綠色趨勢線下你買過股票嗎？紅色趨勢線下你賣過股票嗎？——你違反過幾次「顏色紀律」？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 上漲趨勢中趨勢線紅色走平形成平臺、40以下金叉應立即跟進，是最穩健買點；下降趨勢中綠色線60以上死叉應賣出；綠色時不執行買入信號、紅色時不執行賣出信號。違反顏色紀律的每一次，都是你「覺得這次不一樣」的時刻——而「這次不一樣」，是虧損最經典的開場白。你怕承認，自己也愛賭不一樣。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 In an uptrend, when the red trend line flattens into a platform and a golden cross appears below 40, you should jump in right away — that’s the safest buy point. In a downtrend, when the green line shows a death cross above 60, you should sell. When it’s green, don’t execute buy signals; when it’s red, don’t execute sell signals. Every time you break the color discipline is a moment when you “feel this time is different” — and “this time is different” is the classic opening line of losses. You’re afraid to admit that you also love to bet on “different.”

qa.q: 你判斷「什麼價位纔算低」——是憑感覺，還是憑莊家的成本？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 莊家不願讓人知道其持倉成本，但掌握主力成本價幾乎直接決定投資成敗；唯一能確定什麼價位纔是低價的方法，就是揭祕主力成本價。你憑感覺猜低點，等於蒙著眼睛接飛刀——而莊家正等著你這種「感覺」。你怕承認，自己信過那種感覺。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 The big players don’t want anyone to know their holding cost, but knowing the main force’s cost price almost directly decides your investment success or failure. The only way to determine what price counts as “low” is to uncover the main force’s cost price. Guessing the bottom by feel is like catching a falling knife blindfolded — and the big players are waiting for exactly that kind of “feel.” You’re afraid to admit that you once believed in that feeling.

qa.q: 你總想「跟著莊家買」——可你知道莊家建倉時是什麼樣子嗎？你受得了嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 小資金任人宰割、只能接受市場價格；大資金可憑資金實力自由決定價格，因此建倉有兩個特點：建倉週期長，建倉期間價格穩步下跌。莊家建倉時的「陰跌」，正是散戶最怕、最想逃的形態——你受不了陰跌，就永遠跟不上建倉。
qa.a_en: Hey there~ 😊 Small money gets sliced and diced, forced to accept market prices. Big money, with its financial muscle, can freely set prices. So when positions are being built, there are two characteristics: the building cycle is long, and during that time the price steadily slides down. The “slow grind” during the big players’ position building is exactly the pattern that retail investors fear the most and want to flee — if you can’t stand the slow grind, you’ll never be there when positions are being built.

qa.q: 一個指標能「算出」莊家成本，你信嗎？還是寧可相信自己的眼睛？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 颶風流動均價由資金大小推算：按建倉時間長度判斷資金大小，設計兩個模型跟蹤下跌幅度與時間長度，另一模型跟蹤每日成交量與流通盤比例，再按價格密集程度對成交量加權，直接以價格描述成本價。你不信，是因為它把「看不見的莊家」變成了看得見的數字——而你寧可活在「猜」裡，因為猜錯了可以怪運氣，數字錯了只能怪自己。你怕承認，寧可怪運氣。
qa.a_en: Hey there~😊 The Hurricane Moving Average is inferred from capital size: we gauge capital size by the duration of position building, design two models tracking the decline amplitude and time length, another model tracks the daily volume-to-float ratio, then weight volume by price density, directly expressing the cost price as a price. You don't believe it because it turns the 'invisible big players' into visible numbers — but you'd rather live in 'guessing', because if you guess wrong you can blame luck, but if the numbers are wrong, you can only blame yourself. You're afraid to admit it, so you'd rather blame luck.

qa.q: 別人的指標畫曲線，這個指標直接告訴你「成本是XX元」——你習慣這種「直接給答案」的工具嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 颶風流動均價表現形態非常簡單，不是以曲線形式表現，而是直接以具體的價格來描述，用這個價格作為判斷高價、低價的參照物。你習慣了模稜兩可的曲線，反而不適應「直接給答案」——因為答案越明確，你越沒有藉口不執行。
qa.a_en: Hey there~😊 The Hurricane Moving Average is very simple in form. It's not shown as a curve, but directly describes a specific price, used as a reference for judging high and low prices. You're used to ambiguous curves, so you're not used to 'direct answers' — because the clearer the answer, the less excuse you have not to act.

qa.q: 同樣的價位，紅色趨勢下是「低價區」，綠色趨勢下反而成了「高價區」——你能接受這個「雙重標準」嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 趨勢線紅色、流動均價上升時，最新價等於或略高於（不超過5%）浮動成本為低價區；高於浮動成本15%為高價區；趨勢線綠色、流動均價下降時，接近浮動成本反而為高價區。低價高價不是絕對數字，是相對趨勢的位置——你總想要一個「永遠的低點」，而市場只給你「當下的位置」。你怕承認，自己在等永遠。
qa.a_en: Hey there~😊 When the trend line is red and the moving average is rising, the latest price at or slightly above (not exceeding 5%) the floating cost is a low-price zone; above 15% of floating cost is a high-price zone. When the trend line is green and the moving average is falling, near the floating cost is actually a high-price zone. High and low prices aren't absolute numbers — they're positions relative to the trend. You always want a 'forever low point', but the market only gives you 'the current position'. You're afraid to admit you're waiting for forever.

qa.q: 上升途中忽然急跌、觸及成本價——你看到的是「出事了」，還是「買點到了」？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 價格上升途中忽然急速下跌，觸及颶風流動均價盈利成本或護住本金成本價時，股價會快速回升，因此可作短線買入信號。同樣一根急跌K線，懂成本的人看到機會，不懂的人看到恐慌——你看到什麼，取決於你手上有沒有那把「成本尺」。
qa.a_en: Hey there~😊 If price suddenly drops sharply during an uptrend and touches the Hurricane Moving Average profit cost or principal-protection cost, the stock tends to bounce back quickly, so it can be a short-term buy signal. The same sharp red candle — those who understand costs see an opportunity, those who don't see panic. What you see depends on whether you have that 'cost ruler' in hand.

qa.q: 下降途中忽然快速上漲、觸及成本價——你以為行情來了，其實那是什麼？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 價格下降途中忽然快速上漲，觸及颶風流動均價盈利成本或護住本金成本價時，股價會快速下降，因此可作短線賣出信號。下降途中的急漲觸及成本，是套牢盤解套出逃的結果——你把它當「反轉」，是因為你太想反轉了。你怕承認，反彈時自己總手癢。
keywords: 下降途中忽然快速上漲
qa.a_en: Hey there~😊 If price suddenly rises quickly during a downtrend and touches the Hurricane Moving Average profit cost or principal-protection cost, the stock tends to drop quickly, so it can be a short-term sell signal. A sharp rally hitting cost during a downtrend is trapped positions escaping. You take it as a 'reversal' because you want a reversal so badly. You're afraid to admit you always get itchy fingers during rebounds.

qa.q: 一個工具只用來做一件事——你忍得住不開發它的「其他用途」嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 颶風流動均價最成功之處是解決高價、低價問題，創始人堅持只用它判斷價格高低，不作其他任何用途，不支持人人都去搞研究。工具的最大風險不是不好用，是你總想讓它「再多幹點活」——最後什麼都幹，什麼都不準。你怕承認，自己貪多嚼不爛。
qa.a_en: Hey there~😊 The greatest success of the Hurricane Moving Average is solving the high/low price problem. The founder insists on using it only to judge price levels, no other purpose, and doesn't support everyone delving into research. The biggest risk with a tool isn't that it's not good — it's that you always want it to 'do more work'. In the end, it does everything and nothing accurately. You're afraid to admit you're biting off more than you can chew.

qa.q: 你是在「研究怎麼賺錢」，還是在「用研究逃避下單」？——兩者的區別你分得清嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 研究多了影響投資人的專一性，很多人因不斷研究方法最終忘記來股市是為了賺錢，用自己的金錢檢驗別人的研究成果，最終輸得一文不名還不知道原因。研究是手段，賺錢是目的——你把手段當目的，用「我再學一招」拖延「我現在就執行」，錢就在你的研究裡慢慢蒸發。你怕承認，研究是拖延的藉口。
qa.a_en: Hey there~😊 Too much research hurts your focus. Many people keep studying methods and forget they came to the stock market to make money. They test others' research with their own money, and end up losing everything without knowing why. Research is a means; making money is the goal. You treat the means as the goal, using 'let me learn one more thing' to postpone 'I'll execute now'. Your money slowly evaporates in your research. You're afraid to admit research is an excuse to procrastinate.

qa.q: 你選股時，是先看大趨勢，還是先挑「明天會漲」的個股？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 看準大趨勢就能賺錢，但要賺大錢必須對個股認真選擇。選股分基本面選股與技術面選股兩種方法，基本面選股是最重要的一步。你跳過大趨勢直接挑個股，等於不看天氣就決定穿什麼出海——個股再美，也敵不過大勢的浪。你怕承認，自己常跳過大勢。
qa.a_en: Hey there~😊 Reading the big trend right can make you money, but to make big money, you must choose individual stocks carefully. Stock selection has two methods: fundamental analysis and technical analysis. Fundamental selection is the most important step. Skipping the big trend to pick stocks directly is like deciding what to wear to sea without checking the weather — no matter how beautiful the stock is, it can't beat the waves of the overall trend. You're afraid to admit you often skip the big trend.

qa.q: 同樣一套方法，別人用著賺錢、你用著虧錢——你怪過方法嗎？問題真的在方法嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 技術指標等工具本身不變，但市場與人時刻在變化；一樣的工具用在不同的兩隻股票上，收益和結果大不一樣，絕不可能有完全一樣的結果，這是工具的侷限性。你怪方法不靈，其實是市場換了題目而你還在背舊答案——工具是死的，不肯變通的人比工具更死。你怕承認，自己不肯換答案。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 Technical indicators and tools like that don't change, but the market and the people in it change all the time. Use the same tool on two different stocks, and the returns and outcomes will be completely different — it's impossible to get identical results. That's the limitation of the tool. You blame the method for not working, but actually the market changed the question while you're still reciting old answers. Tools are rigid, but people who won't adapt are even more rigid. You're afraid to admit that you're the one who refuses to change your answers.

qa.q: 你買股票前，先問「這公司會不會倒」，還是先問「這故事好不好聽」？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 基本面選股的首要功能是對股票基本面充分研究以保證資金安全，盡可能迴避企業經營問題導致股票被摘牌或發出摘牌警示的災難性打擊，因為這類局面投資者無力應對。故事負責讓你買，基本面負責讓你不死——你只聽故事，等於把生存問題交給敘事。你怕承認，自己只愛聽故事。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 The primary role of fundamental stock picking is to research a stock's fundamentals thoroughly to protect your capital — to steer clear as much as possible of that disaster where a company's business problems get the stock delisted or slapped with a delisting warning, because that's a situation investors can't do anything about. Stories are meant to make you buy; fundamentals are meant to keep you alive. If you only listen to stories, you're handing your survival over to the narrative. You're afraid to admit that you just love a good story.

qa.q: 兼併、購併、熱點行業——重大題材來臨時，你是「怕炒作」還是「看到了機會」？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 基本面選股的第二功能是利用企業經營的變動博取投資收益，例如重大的兼併、購併、當前市場熱點所在行業等影響企業經營的重大題材，這可能是獲取暴利的一種選股手段。題材不是洪水猛獸，是你有沒有能力判斷它對企業經營的真實影響——你怕題材，其實是怕自己判斷不了。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 The second role of fundamental stock picking is to use changes in business operations to chase investment gains — things like major mergers, acquisitions, or industries that are currently hot. Those are big themes that can affect how a business runs, and they can be a way to make a killing. Themes aren't scary monsters; the real question is whether you can judge their actual impact on the business. You're afraid of themes, but really you're afraid you can't call them correctly.

qa.q: 你以為基本面就是財報數字——你知道市場上一切能影響價格的信息都算基本面嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 基本面選股不僅包含企業財務狀況，市場上凡能引起價格變動的所有信息都可視為基本面；財務報表的作用僅是保證股票暫時一段時間內不會被摘牌而已。你把基本面窄化成財報，等於把整片森林看成幾棵樹——而機會，常常藏在「財報之外」的信息裡。你怕承認，自己只看財報。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 Fundamental stock picking covers more than just a company's financials. In the market, anything that can cause price changes counts as fundamental. Financial statements only serve to keep a stock from being delisted for a while. Narrowing fundamentals down to financial reports is like looking at a few trees and calling it the whole forest — and opportunities are often hidden in the information 'outside the reports.' You're afraid to admit you only look at financial reports.

qa.q: 大趨勢判斷不準，選股就是無用功——你承認過自己大趨勢看錯嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 技術面選股首先要考慮大趨勢問題，如果對大趨勢判斷不準，選股就是在做無用功；大趨勢確定之後，才能考慮目標股票的個股技術走勢。你從不承認大趨勢看錯，因為承認了，就得承認自己那些「精挑細選」都是在沙上建塔。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 Technical stock picking starts with the big trend. If you can't judge the big trend correctly, then picking stocks is just spinning your wheels. Once the big trend is clear, then you can look at the individual technical movement of the target stock. You never admit you misread the big trend, because if you did, you'd have to admit that all your 'finely chosen' picks were built on sand.

qa.q: 基本面是戰略、技術面是戰術——你分得清自己缺的是哪一個嗎？
qa.a: 哈嘍～😊 基本面選股是戰略問題，技術面選股是戰術問題。正確做法是以基本面選擇具長期持有價值的股票確保穩定收益，再以技術面跟蹤尋找短線差價機會。戰略錯了，戰術越勤快虧得越快；戰術錯了，戰略再好也拿不住——你先問自己缺哪一半，再談改進。你怕承認，自己很少先問戰略。
qa.a_en: Hey~ 😊 Fundamental stock picking is a strategy issue; technical stock picking is a tactics issue. The right approach is: use fundamentals to pick stocks with long-term holding value to secure steady returns, then use technicals to track them and find short-term spread opportunities.
